decisions.why: The Rust half that served only the door verb file_left; the Rust land asks scope_split and flight_live in process (kept), and file_left/its constant have no other asker per the recorded census. Removing dead Rust that only served a removed door verb is inside the port; it changes no verdict or output of a live command (FR-002).

decisions.summary: Apply the removal patch kept from T121's landing commit rather than re-deriving it.
decisions.why: A method choice; it decides nothing the spec or request leaves open about scope.

decisions.summary: Premise and done-check: git grep -n of the four names over scripts and rust finds them only in provenance comments and the door's tests (observed 2026-11-12); exits make static, make rust-test, make land green, red set down or ruled through make arbiter-ask.
decisions.why: Enforcement of the removal, not new scope; the figure carries a one-shot label (date and method). Non-blocking note: the stated search space is scripts and rust only - it does not reach the Makefile, tests/, l7r/, .specify/ or specs/, where a name can be held as a string (feature 185); a door caller there would be switched off contrary to FR-003. Running the same git grep over the whole tree before deleting closes that, and does not change this decision's class. ask:449-T82-claims names three Python callers of this door: land.py, replay_owing.py and impl_check.py; the block accounts for the first two and not impl_check.py, which stays a door caller to the phase-3 close. Precondition on the deletion: the census re-run with no pathspec, showing impl_check.py and the Makefile ask none of the four names.

decisions.summary: File T125 under the GM's 2026-11-12 pre-approval: target the full hook run's end (idle-tests, the longest suite, started 19.6 s in by roster order), expected saving about 8 s, measured 52.5 s against 59.4 s mean alternated three a side; ordered after T124.
decisions.why: The pre-approval's conditions are a concrete target and a significant measured expected saving, and the task names both and quotes the words, as request.md's 2026-11-12 entry requires; the GM's later priority puts the tests' and landing's time first after T121, and the full hook run is the landing's longest phase. The measured gain is the removal of the baseline's 62-63 s tail (treatment 51.0-54.9 s against 52.4-63.3 s), not a shift of the floor; that is still a concrete measured saving the GM's words cover.

decisions.summary: make hooks-test dispatches its suites to its eight slots longest first by each suite's seconds at its last run, kept beside its stamp (.git/hooks-test/<suite>.s, pass or fail); a never-timed suite first; the general rule rather than naming idle-tests.
decisions.why: A reordering of the same work to cut the run's wall time, the target the pre-approval covers; the general rule was A/B'd equal to the single-suite move and nothing in the request or spec fixes the roster order.

decisions.summary: A suite's kept seconds is a hint to the order alone; a missing or stale one only moves a suite in the queue.
decisions.why: Keeps the new state from touching any verdict; narrows nothing the GM asked for.

decisions.summary: T98's measurement that longest first was slower, on an earlier roster, is superseded by today's measurement.
decisions.why: T98's ordering finding was a session measurement, not a GM requirement; FR-012's T98 asks only that the suites run in parallel, which stays.

decisions.summary: The engine-freeze suite's two roll fixtures wait (5 s bound) for the roll to appear in /proc by name instead of a fixed 0.5 s sleep, so the cases test a running roll and the other-tree case no longer passes vacuously.
decisions.why: A flake the requested reorder exposed (three engine-freeze cases failed in one longest-first run); the block's own 'Kept as it was: every suite, its cases and its checks' pins the cases, and the change removes the other-tree case's vacuous pass rather than altering what it expects. Needed for the requested speed-up to land green, not new behavior.

decisions.summary: Raising PARTS_MAX above two not done: measured no gain (52.8 s at four, 53.4 s at eight against 50.9 s at two).
decisions.why: Declining an unrequested alternative on measurement; the pre-approval licenses only targets with significant measured savings, which this lacked.

decisions.summary: Every suite, its cases and checks, the stamps, HOOKS_JOBS and PARTS_MAX kept as they were.
decisions.why: Preserves all verdicts and the existing parallelism; removes nothing the GM asked to keep.

decisions.summary: T126 is filed under the GM's 2026-11-12 pre-approval: target l7r-gate.sh's per-call cost, expected saving about 12 ms a call, measured saving on the full hook run 46.6 s against 51.5 s mean over twelve alternated runs.
decisions.why: The pre-approval's conditions are a concrete target and a significant measured saving, the task naming both and quoting the GM's words; the block does all three, and the GM's later words put the tests' and the landing's time first. About 10% of the full hook run, five of six pairs favoring the change by 5 to 9 s, re-read from wrap.txt and wrap2.txt (the twelve numbers and both means match the block). The one HEAD run faster than every new run is reported by the block itself. Soft spot, not a finding: performance item 3's 'many hundreds of calls a full hook run' carries a method that does not count calls; the measured A/B, not that estimate, is what the significance rests on. No FR codifies the 2026-11-12 round (FR-012 and SC-007 stop at T116); the request's own sentence on how such a task is filed is the rule, and the block meets it.

decisions.summary: The wrapper reads the account's home from /etc/passwd in its own shell, matching the shell's UID, with getent kept as the fallback where no line matches.
decisions.why: An implementation choice inside the approved target that keeps the same answer (the same account's home); narrows nothing the GM asked for.

decisions.summary: The stale-binary test becomes one find -newer ... -quit over the same sources in place of a bash glob walk with -nt.
decisions.why: FR-002 binds Python-to-Rust ports; this is shell to shell, so FR-002 is cited by analogy rather than as the operative constraint. The change only widens the rebuild trigger (dot files now seen, strictly newer kept), never skips a rebuild the old test asked for, and the block records a touched source still rebuilding. Nothing asked for is narrowed.

decisions.id: D4 l7r-guard.sh left as it is
decisions.summary: The guards' wrapper is not changed, its rust/guard walk measured at 1.6 ms.
decisions.why: The request asks for concrete targets with significant measured savings, not every wrapper; leaving one below that bar applies the GM's condition rather than narrowing it. Recorded precisely: the 1.6 ms covers the walk only, and the bundle does not say whether l7r-guard.sh also runs the getent/id/cut chain (4.7 ms in the gate wrapper), so that part is unmeasured; it is a possible later target, not a narrowing of this one.

decisions.summary: After T125; green is make hooks-test HOOKS_ALL=1 and make land, red recorded and a claim of impossibility ruled through make arbiter-ask; one landing.
decisions.why: Follows the GM's priority on the tests' and the landing's time after the in-progress work; the exits check the requested saving and the unchanged outputs.

decisions.summary: gm_review.py ported whole with no door into the reviews crate, every caller repointed, the .py and bundle_door's gm_review_add_row verb deleted in the same cut

decisions.why: Placement is design; the one-writer result is what ask:449-T82-claims requires, and the census names its search space.

decisions.why: FR-003: no piece runs both; the fixture stood in for the inline Python that no longer runs.

decisions.why: FR-002 and ask:449-usage-text: hand-written usage stays bound; keeping it is the strict reading.

decisions.summary: close_check.py stays Python, run by path from reviewed only on the branch where the GM's box is a feature's last open box, under the T065 clause, gaining a new --reasons-json DIR SPECS mode that writes no usage-log line; T127 filed for its port, the by-path run going when it lands
decisions.why: Adding a mode changes a Python file the GM said is no longer being changed except to delete it. Legitimate because the spec's own placement requires it: ask:449-T067-scope puts close_check.py in phase 3 carrying the T065 clause until ported, and gm_review.py reached it by import, which a Rust caller cannot do (FR-003: a name a command can carry goes by command); the mode only emits, as JSON, what the import returned and keeps the import's no-usage-log behavior, adding no logic, and its run is on a rare branch, never a plain Bash call or Edit. Should the mode compute anything the import did not, this ruling does not cover it. The alternative, porting close_check in the same cut, is phase-3 work the spec allows but does not require of T91, and T127 holds it.

decisions.summary: the arbiter's failure message 'python3 said: <traceback>' becomes 'gm-review said: <why>', two Rust tests in arbiter/tests.rs changed to expect it
decisions.why: The arbiter is not the replaced piece and the fixed words are the Rust arbiter's own; keeping 'python3 said' would name a subprocess that no longer exists after the port. Ruled precedent T87-arbiter-test-message (LEGITIMATE) on the same message pattern. Exit status and verdict unchanged.

decisions.summary: claims-known on a gm-review write failure prints 'gm-review: <why>' where it printed the runner's traceback; exit status unchanged through the same ? of the same function
decisions.why: ask:449-usage-text: an uncaught Python traceback's text is not bound for any port, its exit status and stdout held; the block records the exit path compared at HEAD and in the working tree. Not resting on T87.

decisions.summary: differential of 1,272 cases accepts 8 differences (7 rows holding NaN, 1 integer past 64 bits) and lists divergences no case reaches; in-process callers 55 cases with none
decisions.why: FR-002 binds every case the piece's tests and suites hold: the kept suites (make hooks-test HOOKS_ALL=1, 54 suites) are green and the real queues of all 47 features as stored and reopened match; the 8 are constructed row values no writer produces, and the only writer after the cut is the port. The differential reaches beyond FR-002's bound set rather than excluding a bound case.

decisions.why: The GM 2026-11-12 put the tests' and landing's performance ahead of remaining ports only where a concrete target with a significant measured saving is identified, otherwise 'keep working on the port of the tooling'. The deletion rests on the GM's standing approval quoted in the spec (2026-11-10).

decisions.summary: impl_check.py stays Python (phase 3, its own later port); the Rust runs impl_check.py --missing-json DIR... by path, one process a run and none when no non-grandfathered research-record directory needs it, no usage line; the new mode prints only what missing() returned; stderr carried inside the error on failure, passed through or dropped on success as before.

A logic-free JSON verb on the Python side is the door pattern the spec uses throughout (codeid.py --debug-free-equal, bundle_door, claims_door); impl_check runs in one implementation, so FR-003 holds. The mode leaves with impl_check's own port by that pattern.

decisions.summary: Accept 2 of 117 scratch cases differing: a directory named '٣-x', whose non-ASCII digit Python's int() reads as 3 (pointing the user at make feature-report F=3, a different feature) and the Rust refuses. Re-derived from results-scratch.json: 'differ': 2, both this name; results-real/push/tick/gm/impl all 'differ': 0, seen totals 1,469+22+9+8+117+20 = 1,645.
decisions.why: Ruled here on FR-002's own scope, not on its written exception (which covers a port that stops refusing correct work, not one that starts refusing a mis-parse) and not on the T91/T118 precedent, which the block cites without an ask: id. FR-002 binds 'every case its tests and its suites hold'; this input is one the session's harness constructed, held by no kept test or suite case, and every real feature directory in the clone (1,469 cases, both forms, real and empty grandfathered lists) and every real push range (22) match. The request's purpose - a Rust codebase that decides as the Python did on the work it actually does - is intact; the divergence is disclosed in the plan.

decisions.summary: Known divergences no case reaches: a lone surrogate, nesting past 128 or 1e400 in a measurements.json, a directory name not UTF-8; plus the normalizations (stderr from the first Traceback, the usage line's utc, each side's scratch path).
decisions.why: Adjudicated apart from the '٣-x' case: none is a case any kept test or suite holds, and the real tree reaches none (every real directory's measurements.json is read in the 1,469 real cases with no difference), so FR-002's binding set is untouched. The traceback normalization is ask:449-usage-text's ruling that a traceback's text is not bound; utc and scratch paths are run-specific, not outputs.

decisions.summary: check tool-signals reads `log usage` as a record marker, skips Rust test files, and names the command in its fix
decisions.why: the check now reads less (Rust test files). Its purpose is that every registered tool records its usage; a test file is not a tool and holds no tool's record marker, while read literally the check would refuse the port itself on fixture scratch names. The block measured every registered tool still found (exit 0, suite green), and old-form markers are still accepted, so the purpose is intact.

decisions.summary: test-gate-write-hooks.sh no longer copies the deleted preflight.py; clone-sync context drops the python field nothing read once the run is in process

decisions.why: timestamps and generated file names are not comparable outputs; argparse text and traceback text are exactly what ask:449-usage-text rules unbound, exit status and stdout held.

decisions.summary: Each make-figures command that runs a script or Python test (python3 <file>, python3 -c, make spec-harness, make test-file, make -C .claude/skills/diagram) and fails today or invokes deleted code is retired to <retired: ask:449-phase3-remainder, why> with values kept, its script and any harness/counts file only it ran deleted: 27 files, 4,367 entries across 18 features; 387's four placeholders, 276's measure_before_five.py and 340's harness.py join

'Fails today' was tested once in a scratch clone with a 90 s bound; the block itself notes a fresh clone lacks untracked renders, and it does not show for each fails-today-only retiree that its failure is clone-independent - no wrongly retired script can be named from the bundle, so this is noted, not ruled.

decisions.summary: About 70 failing make-figures commands that run no file (35 greps of old skill paths in 261, greps/ls on moved text or untracked SVGs, prose with shell syntax, 375's three make feature-report on transcripts no longer on disk, one prose entry in 449's own file) are reported and not retired
decisions.why: The ruling's sentence literally reaches 'a command make figures runs that fails when run today', so this narrows the accepted spec. It is legitimate on purpose, not by completing anyone's thought: the GM's request is a Python-to-Rust port and the 2026-11-09 words are about not porting unused past-feature harnesses; FR-001's rewrite duty covers only recorded measurements that RUN Python. A failing grep, ls or prose entry runs no Python and no file, imposes no port, and retiring it serves no clause of the GM's request - it would be unrequested cleanup. The ruling's own words bound its subject to files: the consequence is 'its file deleted unported', the counterpart is 'the measurement scripts that run and work are ported (T139)', and the census it rules on is of tracked .py files. Adjudicated separately, the three make feature-report commands run feature_report, which T119 placed on the port and which is reached through make, so no port-or-delete decision rides on them either way (unlike ask:449-T120-retire-375-a7, whose command ran python3 turn_time.py and so was a Python-running measurement FR-001 had to rewrite). The narrowing guts nothing the request asked for.

decisions.summary: The Rust `plan door` subcommand keeps bypass-record (plan-gate.sh) and active-task (review_round_hooks.rs) for callers that are not Python files.
decisions.why: The ruling deletes scripts/plan_door.py, the Python door, and that happens; the kept verbs are Rust serving non-Python callers, so no Python remains and nothing asked for is held back. Premise, not checkable from the bundle: the block says review_round_hooks.rs asks active-task 'through an inline snippet' and places that caller among 'callers that are not Python files'. This ruling assumes the snippet starts no Python. If it does start Python, that is a phase-1 regression to be raised. It does not change this cut's fidelity.

decisions.summary: --land-check and --resolve kept as commands of the binary; Path.glob and fnmatch empty ranges ported in glob.rs.
decisions.why: Implementation choices that keep FR-002 parity; decide nothing the spec left to the GM.

decisions.summary: The land's message 'tick-task.py raised on <task>' becomes 'the tick raised on <task> (above)'.
decisions.why: FR-002 binds the land's own hand-written words, and this changes them. The ruling rests on the purpose test alone. The cut deletes tick-task.py and runs the tick in process, so keeping the string byte for byte would make the land report that a program no longer in the tree raised. That would be a false output, and it would work against the request's purpose: "making this a Rust codebase instead of a Python codebase". What a reader acts on is unchanged: the task named, the failure, the verdict and the exit. The plan names T87 and T91 as precedent. The bundle does not carry them, so this ruling takes the plan's word for them and does not rest on them. Neither ask:449-usage-text nor ask:449-T92-messages supports the change: both keep a tool's hand-written words bound.

decisions.summary: The first pass's 'tick-task.py --land-check exited N' becomes a raise carrying the crate's own error.
decisions.why: This one is physically impossible to keep: the check now runs in process, so there is no child process and no exit status N to report. The verdict, a raise in the first pass, is kept.

decisions.summary: FR-002 proof: 274 command-line cases and 31 land/task-add cases, none differing, under named normalizations (traceback past its first line, bypass record file name and same-second record split, phase-read clock, the renamed message, AUTO_MERGE, stamps, commit ids); five divergences named that no case reaches.
decisions.why: Each normalization is a ruled one (traceback, ask:449-usage-text), clock or identity noise, or the message ruled above. The one raw difference was a same-second timing collision, and it went away on three reruns. The five named divergences are inputs that no test or suite holds, and FR-002 binds only 'every case its tests and its suites hold'. Naming them is disclosure, not an exclusion.

decisions.summary: No recorded measurement runs the deleted files or the three make targets; the constitution keeps its version-history line naming the test file.
decisions.why: FR-001's rewrite-in-the-cut duty is found empty by a stated search; a version-history line is not a runner.

decisions.summary: Lands after T134, whose --sources it asks in process.
decisions.why: Ordering only.

decisions.summary: The Rust reads the gate's active-task JSON itself; a failed run, non-JSON output, a null directory or an empty task hold nothing, a directory and a task go on to the plan-round cap as before.
decisions.why: FR-002: the same verdicts as the Python snippet it replaces. On record: the block derives all four forms from two Python mechanisms (`if d is not None and task`, the raise on bad JSON), so the 'failed run' form's equivalence rests on a failed gate run printing non-JSON stdout; a nonzero exit with valid JSON on stdout is neither named nor pinned. FR-002 binds the cases the tests hold, so this does not block.

decisions.summary: The guard runs `scripts/gates/l7r-gate.sh plan door active-task <root>` as a subprocess rather than calling the gate in-process.
decisions.why: The Python snippet's own shape with the Python removed; FR-001 phase 1 and `ask:449-phase1-tools-by-path` require that a guard start no Python, and with `plan_door.py` deleted in T131 (`ask:449-phase3-remainder`) the hop is Rust end to end. FR-007's one process per tool call governs the guards' fan-out, not a guard asking the gate.

decisions.summary: The guard's tests answer active-task from the gate stub instead of running the snippet under sh, and pin each of the four nothing-forms.
decisions.why: Enforcement of FR-002 (same verdicts) and FR-004 (coverage floor) for the requested port; a check whose only effect is that the ported behavior holds is in scope.

decisions.summary: No other python3 snippet of the guard asks the gate, from `git grep -n "subprocess.run" -- rust/guard/src`; the checks make hooks-test, make static, make rust-test.
decisions.why: Excludes nothing requested: the task claims only this hop, and FR-001 phase 1 still owes any other Python start in the guard. Finding on the search space (not a narrowing): the stated goal is 'a spec-fidelity dispatch starts no Python in the guard', but the grep searches a Python API name inside snippets, not the mechanism. It misses `subprocess.check_output`, `Popen`, `os.system` and any snippet that does not shell out. The waist is the Rust side that starts the interpreter, e.g. `git grep -nE 'python3?\b' -- rust/guard/src`, read hit by hit. The census as a done criterion should use that search.

decisions.summary: Both review_snapshot.py and impl_check.py pass the T81-slices import test (stdlib plus one door each, nothing under interactive/, Mode A or the page writer) and port in phase 3.
decisions.why: ask:449-phase3-remainder places review_snapshot.py with impl_check.py in T132 and orders the import test first; the block records that test with date and method. The earlier rulings that left them as door callers named at the phase-3 close (ask:449-T82-claims for impl_check.py, ask:449-T89-reviews for review_snapshot.py) are superseded by that later ruling, so porting them now is not a departure.

decisions.summary: Snapshot in reviews (calling owed::owed in process); implementation check in claims with --missing-json kept; closing check takes the implementation check as a handed-in function (closing::ImplCheck); the task crate now builds on claims.
decisions.why: Internal placement serving FR-001's port with no door (the ruling says 'no door' by deleting both doors with them). No command form is removed. Design choices of crate layout are not fidelity questions.

decisions.summary: The closing check calls the implementation check in process, so Closing's carried stderr from a separate process goes; a raise still ends in impl_check.missing raised and every caller exits as before.
decisions.why: An internal field, not an output: FR-002 binds what callers see, and the block's differential runs make impl-check with the closing check end to end, the old binary running impl_check.py by path against the new in-process call, over --reasons-json and --push (139 cases, the only differences make's own Makefile-path line). close-check and gm-review hand the same function from the binary.

decisions.summary: make verify's two snapshot lines and make impl-check repointed to l7r-gate.sh; test stand-ins for impl_check.py become Rust function stand-ins; the pair-hooks stub stops forwarding checks-door.
decisions.why: Repointing every caller in the cut is what FR-003 (no piece runs both) and the ruling's deletion of the doors require.

decisions.summary: checks-door and claims-door verbs and claims/door.rs removed; core serve_with/keep_batches, checks-close and the owed, record, bundle and plan doors kept; door tests that were the only cover of four functions move to claims/tests.rs.
decisions.why: ask:449-phase3-remainder: checks_door.py and claims_door.py are deleted with these two files, their last callers; the Rust verbs serving them go with them, and the remaining doors still have callers. Moving the tests keeps FR-004's coverage.

decisions.summary: Claims are read once per repository per run where the Python read them once per directory; answers the same.
decisions.why: An internal efficiency in the spirit of FR-006; FR-002 is held by the differential, not waived.

decisions.summary: make replay-owing's OLD side imports each past commit's own claims_door.py, so a commit after this cut (which has no claims_door.py) cannot be replayed by OLD; the recorded sc001-replay (feature 372's commits) is unchanged and no recorded command replays a later commit.
decisions.why: A tool loses reach it would otherwise have had. Legitimate on two of MODE 1's grounds: keeping it is physically impossible once claims_door.py is gone, and its deletion is mandated by the ruling's own words (ask:449-phase3-remainder: 'claims_door.py deleted with them'), with the GM's standing approval to delete ported Python. The purpose ask:449-T83-scope protected - that make figures can re-run sc001-replay - is intact, and the block shows by git grep over every specs/*/measurements*.json that no recorded command replays a post-cut commit. The limit comes from how T121 ported the OLD side (a Python snippet importing the past commit's door); T132 records it rather than chooses it. The block does not say whether a post-cut OLD replay fails loudly or silently; that is not a fidelity defect, but the record should say which.

decisions.summary: 829 cases, 11 differing: 6 are make's own '*** [...Makefile:685]' line naming the Makefile each side ran with -f; 5 are raises with identical exit, stdout and files whose traceback text above the shared last line differs. Normalizations: stderr from a Traceback line, argparse usage errors on exit 2 and empty stdout, log stamps, bytecode off, dispatch.md by content.
decisions.why: The 6 are harness text (make's own line, from running each side's Makefile with -f), not the tool's output. The 5 and the Traceback and argparse normalizations are exactly FR-002's ruled case ask:449-usage-text: 'an uncaught Python traceback's text is not bound for any port, its exit status and stdout staying held', argparse's generated stderr not bound with exit 2 and empty stdout held. The stamps and bytecode are harness hygiene. Being non-zero, the task is not straight under FR-001c, which is why this review is owed.

decisions.summary: Named divergences no case reaches: a glob character in a map name, non-ASCII digits in a feature number, \x1c-\x1f as whitespace, invalid UTF-8 replacement, --help's full text.
decisions.why: FR-002 binds 'every case its tests and its suites hold'; --help is additionally ruled bound only where a kept test or suite case holds it (ask:449-usage-text). The others are disclosed, not hidden. 'No case reaches' is a statement about the 829 harness cases and the held suites, as the block says; it is not a claim that live data cannot contain them, and I did not verify it beyond the block.

decisions.summary: Census at the cut: only provenance comments and replay_owing.rs' OLD snippet name the four files; no specs/*/measurements*.json command names any of them in command, import or -m form, so no recorded measurement is rewritten.

Noted: the lossy read and the line scan could pass where the Python would have errored (invalid UTF-8, invalid TOML, a commented fail_under), on inputs not present.

decisions.summary: scripts/measure/tooling_reuse_time.py deleted unported and its three commands in feature 383's measurements.json retired (values kept), in this commit rather than T140's.
decisions.why: Narrows FR-001's replace-every-Python-file by deleting one unported. Not legitimate on the quoted Q5 condition alone ('if its commands fail today'): before this cut tests/tooling held tests, so the commands failed only because this cut empties the tree. decisions.summary: The differential normalizes: Traceback stderr; argparse's exit-2 usage text; the quoted regex-library text after 'KEY is not a regular expression - '; session ids and run-log names; the guard-log file name, utc and command; a goals line's utc; the stub's environment keys; the case path in the long cases. The quoted library error text falls under ask:449-T066-json-message, which keeps the fixed words bound. Ids, timestamps and pid-based file names are nondeterministic. The harness (diff.py's NORMALIZED list) says the runner's guard-log 'command' is the process's own argv: the generator naming itself, deleted in this cut, which ask:449-T135-generator rules, though the block does not cite it. Reserve's 'command' differs only by the harness's old/ directory. The listed divergences lie outside the cases FR-002 binds (the cases its tests and suites hold).
