decisions.summary: The task runs after T135 in one landing. It exits on make static, rust-test, hooks-test HOOKS_ALL=1 and land, and a claim that it cannot be done goes to make arbiter-ask.
decisions.why: Procedure inside the plan's own process. Nothing that was asked is narrowed.

decisions.summary: Every ticked task with an id (lowercase `- [x] Tnn`) and its indented lines moves to tasks-done.md, unless it holds an open box; the GM-review box, headings, Occasions and prose stay; no recent ticked tasks kept; blocks byte for byte in id order; one pointer line, no per-block marker.
decisions.why: The GM asked for tooling that moves completed tasks out of tasks.md so it stops eating tokens. A ticked task that still holds an open box is not completed work (it holds a landing), and the GM box is an open review state, not a finished task, so keeping them is not a carve-out from the request. The tick itself treats only lowercase [x] as ticked and writes it that way, so every task finished through the tooling moves. Moving all finished tasks instead of keeping a few recent ones reads 'old completed tasks' at its widest and serves the token purpose.

decisions.summary: Every tick archives all of its feature's ticked tasks, plan section or not; make plan-archive and `tick --archive` move them by hand; 449 archived in the cut; closed features are not backfilled; the tick-archive usage line is recorded on every tick.
decisions.why: 'Automatically move' is carried by the tick. The purpose is long-running features worked on now, and each open feature clears at its next tick. The request asks for the mechanism, not a migration of closed features, so not backfilling does not take any case away from it, and the manual command stays available for any feature. The tool-yield shift is a side effect, not new behavior.

decisions.summary: One reader/mover in the guard's shared::speckit::tasks; the readers that need ticked tasks (state, approval at_rev, plan checks, next id, already-ticked, spec lint, report) read both files; readers of open tasks only keep reading tasks.md, from a stated grep census.
decisions.why: Without this, the archive would break readers: a feature would read as reopened, an archived id could be handed out again, and so on. Wiring the readers to the moved file is what makes the requested move correct (FR-003, one implementation). The enumeration states its search space.

decisions.summary: The tick's block end becomes any heading (it was only `## `, so a `###` heading got swallowed and 449's T001/T005/T070 were misplaced, repaired before the archive; closed 383/417 left as history); a refused land batch removes the tasks-done.md/plan-done.md its tick created.
decisions.why: The archive moves blocks by the tick's own block boundary, so a boundary that swallows a heading would carry that heading into tasks-done.md. A refused landing that leaves the new archive file untracked would leave the tree half-moved. Both fixes exist only so that the requested move is correct. Leaving closed features' history alone is not a narrowing of anything the GM asked for.

decisions.summary: A before/after comparison over every feature archived in a copy (1,001 outputs, none differing); the archived lookup reads lowercase [x] alone to match the tick's rule; an end-to-end make run; 449's sizes; static, rust-test and hooks-test green.
decisions.why: These are checks that only fail if the requested archive changes what any reader answers, or if it does not happen. That is enforcement of the request and FR-002, not a property the GM never mentioned. The lowercase rule keeps the archived lookup consistent with the tick, so it is not a carve-out.

decisions.summary: Done before the phase-4 slices, which file their tasks into the archived tasks.md; budget one landing.
decisions.why: This is sequencing within the feature. It takes nothing out of the request.

decisions.summary: guard_log reaches the Rust through the gate binary (l7r-gate log guard), not the guard binary through l7r-guard.sh; the one hook-time caller runs under L7R_GATE_STALE_OK=1 and a new L7R_GATE_NO_BUILD=1 seam so it never waits on a build
decisions.why: A choice of route for the port FR-001 and ask:449-phase4-slices Q12 require; it keeps no Python and changes no output. The loop through l7r-guard.sh's no-binary path is the stated reason. The no-build seam keeps hook-time cost off a compile, which serves the request's own purpose (hook latency, the GM 2026-11-07).

decisions.summary: On l7r-guard.sh's no-binary path, when the gate has no binary either, the failed-open entry is written by a new shell writer, scripts/hooks/lib/failed-open-log.sh (jq, or printf without jq), byte for byte HEAD's Python entry; every other entry goes through the one Rust writer
decisions.why: FR-001 says the Python is replaced by Rust, and this one path is replaced by shell instead. Running Rust there is physically impossible: the path exists because no binary is built. The only other choices are keeping Python (the request refuses that) or dropping the entry (an FR-002 output lost, and the only record that the guards did not run). The request's purpose is no Python, and that holds on this path too. The writer is confined to that one path, and the differential's 1,028 no-binary cases match HEAD.

decisions.summary: Two disclosed edges of the shell writer: a lower-case float literal (nan) that jq reads and Python's JSON rejects, and, without iconv, a non-UTF-8 input that also holds a real U+FFFD
decisions.why: FR-002 binds every case the tests and suites hold. Neither edge is a held case: upper-case NaN and the payload shapes are held, run on the no-binary path, and match (nogate-payload 125/0 in results.json). No held case is excluded or changed. The edges are disclosed in the file header, on a path reached only when nothing is built, and on input Claude Code's JSON serializer does not emit. If a held case is ever found among them, this becomes a narrowing.

decisions.summary: pyjson::loads keeps integers past u64, NaN, Infinity and floats past a double's range as Python's JSON did, written back bare by pyjson::dumps; serde_json arbitrary_precision is rejected because it would change every crate's numbers
decisions.why: This serves FR-002 (the Python's outputs). It is kept local so that no other crate's output moves (FR-002 for every other piece). Wording only: the decision says 'scoped to the door' while the approach says 'no door'. That is an inconsistency in the text, not a decision.

decisions.summary: pyjson::ascii_string escapes 0x7f as ensure_ascii does, changing log run, log bypass, escape take and the guard log for that character; the guards' entries share the shell's writer; the shared resolver (also read by clone-sync routing) takes clone-resolve.sh's real-path, dot-file, whitespace and empty-variable semantics
decisions.why: Each change moves an already-ported Rust writer or resolver toward the Python it replaced. Python's ensure_ascii escapes 0x7f: its ESCAPE_ASCII class is everything outside space to tilde. So the old core test pinned an FR-002 divergence. One writer and one resolver serve FR-003 and FR-001c's one implementation. No held case of any suite or crate moves (54 suites and 23 crates green), and live routing does not move because /diagram and the clone are not symlinks.

decisions.summary: l7r-gate takes its arguments as bytes: log guard decodes them as Python's surrogateescape did; any other subcommand given non-UTF-8 exits 101 with a message where it panicked
decisions.why: For log guard this is FR-002 fidelity to the shell's Python. For the other subcommands the exit status stays 101, and only a Rust panic's text becomes a message. That text is no output FR-002 binds (by analogy with ask:449-usage-text's traceback ruling), and no held case changes.

decisions.summary: The FR-002 proof is HEAD's shell against the new one: exit, stdout, stderr and every file written compared, normalizing an entry's utc, its file name and a bypass record's name and utc
decisions.why: Carries FR-002. The normalizations remove time values only. HEAD's guardlog.sh named entries with date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%S%6N (microseconds), and the new Rust writer's header gives microseconds too, so the shell's entries keep the Python's name form and only the unreproducible timestamp digits are normalized. FIGURE FINDING (not a narrowing): the block's '2,194 cases' with 'the guard log 1,167 (... 8 log-directory cases ...)' and 'the spec-kit functions 364' does not reconcile with its own run. results.json gives 2,194 = 1,166 guard-log cases (logdir 7, not 8) + 1,028 no-binary cases, and the 364 spec-kit cases are a separate run (results-speckit.json, 364/0). All differ in none, but the block's figures must be corrected: 1,166 and 7, and 2,194 stated as excluding the 364 (2,558 in all).

decisions.summary: clone-resolve.sh (one caller, guardlog.sh) and common.sh's resolve_template_content (no caller) are deleted unported; test-clone-sync-hooks.sh's one clone-resolve.sh case now checks the name through guard_log
decisions.why: FR-001 places clone-resolve.sh with guardlog.sh in phase 3, and Q12 names both files' Python. Code nothing runs is deleted rather than ported (the GM 2026-11-09). The census names its git grep and its search space (scripts/, .specify/, rust/, tests/, the Makefile, .claude/). The rerouted test case keeps its assertion and expected verdict, only its entry point moves.

decisions.summary: The inline-census-sites figure (57 recorded, 41 now) is left to the arbiter to retire or re-record; speckit.manifest.json's stale hash of common.sh is left; measure audit's load() defect on a lone \udcXX is named as not this task's
decisions.why: These are deferred or out of task, not decided in a way that narrows the request. The figure goes to the arbiter. The reader defect belongs to an already-landed port and no entry triggers it today. The manifest hash rests on an unmeasured 'nothing reads it' but decides nothing within T143's scope.

decisions.summary: guard_log costs 47 ms against 8 ms (no hook input) and 67 ms against 8 ms (with one), paid only where a guard or gate refuses or is escaped
decisions.why: This is a measurement report with a one-shot label (date and method). It decides nothing.

decisions.summary: Port the record core (17 record modules, sources.py, content.py) as the gate crate `research` with no production caller; the Python stays the implementation and is not deleted here
decisions.why: FR-003 (the Python remains the one that runs until its replacement passes; no piece runs both) and FR-002 ('before that Python is deleted') carry this without the ruling. ask:449-phase4-slices Q1 was cited but its text was not in the bundle, so the plan's paraphrase of it was not relied on. Module count and slice assignment checked against the phase-4 census (17 record/ rows plus sources.py and content.py, all slice S1).

decisions.summary: Reuse the Rust already present and fold duplicated helpers (cited-URL cleaning and url id, blocked list, html.escape, trailing-punctuation trim) into one copy; keep units::restored and the raw readers of five checks apart because they port different Python or refuse less
decisions.why: FR-003's one implementation. Keeping the near-duplicates apart is done expressly so no check's verdict moves (FR-002); that is fidelity, not a carve-out.

decisions.summary: Eleven Python functions nothing calls are not ported and go with their files
decisions.why: Narrows FR-001's 'every Python file replaced' at function level, but the GM's own words (2026-11-09: 'I don't think we need to port the past feature harnesses if those are not still used') imply not porting unused code, and an uncalled function has no verdict or output FR-002 could bind. The census states its search space (git grep of each name over the whole tree, which reaches Makefiles, shell and registries holding a name as a string). The eleven are not named in the block; the ruling rests on the stated method, not on a checked list.

decisions.summary: archive_first_hooks (six entities decoded) and blocked_fetch_hooks (none) both now call the shared url_id, which decodes every entity as the Python hm_fetch.archived did
decisions.why: Changes two landed guards on live input, but toward the Python they replaced, which is FR-002's direction, and removes a duplicate (FR-003). Suites unmoved means no suite case holds the affected URL form; that is acceptable here because the change restores the Python's behavior rather than departing from it.

decisions.summary: No process cache: the Python's per-file memo, @cache readers and clear_caches left to each caller; sources::Reader holds a loaded record for its lifetime; notes as ordered pairs, sections as owned trees matched by id
decisions.why: FR-002 binds verdicts and outputs, not memoization or object identity; the replay shows no output differing on the real record. clear_caches' two recorded calls are the replay's skips, consistent with this decision. ask:449-T81-slices was cited but not supplied in the bundle.

decisions.summary: make static's dead check counts pub fn names over every .rs including tests, so the uncalled library passes it; no caller added for the check
decisions.why: An observation of an existing check; nothing is relaxed or added.

decisions.summary: Recorded-run differential over every public function: 378,360 calls, 118 functions, none differing; byte offsets compared as character offsets (the refusal still printing the character offset); a library's own words compared up to them; 336 calls inside a load covered by the load's output
decisions.why: Re-read replay.out: TOTAL 378360, 0 differing, 119 functions listed of which 118 called (clear_caches 0); split_originals 163 files same bytes. Offsets are comparison-side only; library words are ask:449-T066-json-message, inside FR-002. Two comparison details the block does not state: the replay skips 339 calls, not 336 (the other three are clear_caches' 2, covered by T144-no-cache, and one split.heading_id call with offset -1 from the driver's own sweep input bad.find('<h2'), which no caller passes), and its same_error treats any two OS-error kinds (OSError, FileNotFoundError, IsADirectoryError, NotADirectoryError) as equal without comparing their messages. Neither touches a case a test or suite holds, so FR-002 still holds; both should be stated in the record rather than left in the harness.

decisions.summary: A KeyError's message compared with its quotes stripped
decisions.why: This is a case changed in comparison, which FR-001c names. Legitimate for this slice only: the library has no caller, so no bound output moves, and a KeyError the Python left uncaught is a traceback FR-002 does not bind. The plan does not say whether any Python caller prints str(e) of these KeyErrors; where one does, that caller's wiring slice (S5, S11 or S12) must reproduce the quotes, and this ruling does not release it.

decisions.summary: host neither drops tabs nor applies urlsplit's NFKC check
decisions.why: Ruled apart from NaN. A known departure from the Python, legitimate for the unwired library only: no production caller exists (FR-003), and FR-002 binds the cases tests and suites hold, which none of these is. 'No real case reaches' was measured against the record's cited and attempted URLs, not against the live fetch URLs the blocked-fetch guard reads, and this host sits beside the blocked-domain list. S5, which wires blocked.py, owes its own decision on closing the divergence or ruling on it, and this ruling does not decide that.

decisions.summary: JSON NaN, which Python's json accepts, is not accepted
decisions.why: Ruled apart from host. The readers read files the tooling writes; the sweep covered every record file and found none holding NaN; no test or suite case holds it (FR-002's scope); and nothing changes now, because there is no production caller.

decisions.summary: Unicode digits read as Python's int() reads them, found by the sweep and fixed
decisions.why: Brings the Rust to the Python's output (FR-002).

decisions.summary: S5 deletes archive, blocked, site_notes and source_tags; S11 the other record modules and sources.py; S12 content.py
decisions.why: Scheduling under FR-003. Checked against p4census/census.tsv python_leaves_in: every row agrees.

decisions.summary: Exits, budget and checks (make static, rust-test, hooks-test, land); no constant moved; not performance work
decisions.why: Holds the coverage floor and gate that FR-001c keeps on every task; it decides nothing beyond the spec.

decisions.summary: The eight tools are ported, wired to every make, Rust and suite caller, and five are deleted. bundle_door's run/passages/save_cached verbs, owed_door's mb and record_door's americanize_json/moved_only retire with their callers.
decisions.why: This is not a narrowing: it ports and deletes more, and sooner, than the minimum. ask:449-phase4-slices' 'library with no production caller' is the shape that makes a slice straight under FR-001c, and this task keeps its review instead. The earlier rulings already put the switch at this cut: T80-order ('Rust downloads running reserve-prefix.py by path until T81 lands'), T81-slices (quote_verbatim's Rust callers 'by command until then'), T88-bundles ('each verb leaves the runner when its owner ports'), and T81-hm-record / T87 (a door is deleted with its last caller). FR-003's one writer is kept by bullet 3.

decisions.summary: translation.rs's cache key becomes the sha1 of a version string plus the Rust parser's sources (include_str!). A bump of the pinned normalization crate needs a manual bump of the string.
decisions.why: This keeps the Python's rule that a parser edit invalidates the cache. The Python's key, which hashed the .py bytes, did not cover a library upgrade either, so the reach is unchanged.

decisions.summary: sources.py, attempts.py and reserve-prefix.py become thin forwarders to the Rust writers. Their command lines, ledger writers, seed, import_saves, CachedPages and key cap are removed. attempts.write refuses the attempts log. Each shared file gets one named writer, and 'escape take' retires.
decisions.why: This is FR-003 and ask:449-T86-door applied as written (a name a command can carry goes by command). The refusal in attempts.write only enforces the one-writer rule. No importer passes it the attempts log (the importers' calls were read). The uncited lists keep the Python as their one writer.

decisions.summary: A CPython HTML parser port, decoder and case-fold tables generated from CPython, unicode-normalization pinned to match Python 3.14.4's NFKC, and curl as an external transport. ParseCache is not carried. An edit to the kept Python makes the same change in the Rust.
decisions.why: These choices exist to hold FR-002's outputs. On ParseCache, T81-slices lets each Rust caller keep or drop caching on its own measurement, its differential matching either way. The same-change clause is phase4-slices' own words.

decisions.summary: record_prepass.py and style_prepass.py are ported in this cut, beside T80-order's six.
decisions.why: T88-bundles makes them T85's. T81-slices names that cluster T85, and phase4-slices folds T85 into S2/S3. Their bundle_door verbs leave with them.

decisions.summary: Two fixes. S1's source_tags.rs now raises on a non-UTF-8 vocabulary, and translation-owed now fails on a root that is not a directory, both as the Python did.
decisions.why: Both restore FR-002 parity with the Python that existed before the port. Neither changes an expected verdict away from the Python.

decisions.summary: FR-002 difference: reserve on a source-tags.json that is not JSON quotes the Rust parser's words inside the Python's fixed message.
decisions.why: This is exactly ask:449-T066-json-message's class. The harness record shows exit 2 on both sides and 'reserve: source-tags.json: not JSON (' ... ')' identical, with only serde's text inside the parentheses differing.

decisions.summary: FR-002 difference: make apply-edits with a missing reply has the same exit and exception kind (FileNotFoundError), and only its message text differs.
decisions.why: In the Python this was an uncaught exception. ask:449-usage-text says an uncaught traceback's text is not bound for any port, while exit status and stdout stay held, and the block holds both.

decisions.summary: Normalization (216 cases): the text inside '<urlopen error ...>' is curl's where Python gave its errno text. Exit, stderr frame, JSON report and the UNFETCHABLE verdict are the same.
decisions.why: T066-json-message binds verdict, exit status, location and fixed words, and lets through a library's own error text quoted inside a fixed message. curl is the transport in the role the Python's socket library had. The harness regex replaces only the text after '<urlopen error ', and the dead-host run done raw on both sides showed everything else equal, so no output the tool writes itself is hidden.

decisions.summary: Normalization: argparse's exit-2 text and an uncaught traceback's text are compared by refusal and by exception kind.
decisions.why: This is ask:449-usage-text. The harness's exit-2 rule is broader than the ruling, since it would also collapse a hand-written parser.error(). I checked HEAD's eight files in the harness's ref copy: none calls parser.error or exits 2 by hand, and their hand-written stderr lines start with the tool's name, which neither branch of the normalizer collapses. So it hides only unbound text.

decisions.summary: The key-cap escape's guard-log 'command' field names 'l7r-gate record reserve' where it named reserve-prefix.py.
decisions.why: The Python wrote the field as ' '.join(sys.argv), its own invocation (reserve-prefix.py:59 in the harness's HEAD copy). The Rust records its own invocation by the same definition, so the field's meaning is unchanged. T135-generator's condition holds for the code that writes the entry, since the key cap is removed from the Python in this cut. Keeping 'reserve-prefix.py' would name a process that no longer writes the entry.

decisions.summary: Timestamps and the guard-log entry's file name (UTC-microsecond plus pid) are normalized.
decisions.why: These differ between two runs of the same side, so they are not outputs either implementation reproduces.

decisions.summary: Timings are recorded and not held. quote-verbatim is faster, while the prepass/style sweeps (230 s vs 337 s) and the archive sweep (41 s vs 88 s) are slower.
decisions.why: The spec binds timing per phase (FR-010, SC-001..003), not per port, and FR-002 binds outputs. Recording the figures does not narrow a requirement.

decisions.summary: No measurements.json command runs the eight. 375's two one-shot rows that name three of them as timing keys keep their values as that day's record.
decisions.why: FR-001's rewrite rule covers a recorded command that runs a ported file. Those rows run 'make check-bundle', which stays, so nothing that runs Python is left unrewritten.

decisions.summary: archive.py's logic ported to a new gate crate `archive`; its browser a new crate rust/browser/ (l7r-browser serve and crop) outside the gate's and guard's builds, no gate or guard crate depending on it
decisions.why: FR-001 / ask:449-T80-order (4) as amended by ask:449-T146-browser: a client of its own in its own binary, out of the guards' and gate's build path; ask:449-phase4-slices S3a.

decisions.summary: The browser client speaks the DevTools protocol over --remote-debugging-pipe itself, launched with Playwright's switches and page setup, instead of chromiumoxide or headless_chrome
decisions.why: Exactly what the round arbiter ruled in ask:449-T146-browser (2026-11-16), written into FR-001 and T80-order (4): a DevTools-pipe client of its own, lighter than both named crates (9 against 92 and 118, one-shot labeled).

decisions.summary: scripts/record/glyph_crop.py ported to `l7r-browser crop` and deleted in this cut; depiction.rs runs it through l7r-gate.sh browser crop
decisions.why: ask:449-phase4-slices: S3a is archive.py and glyph_crop on the one browser crate; ask:449-T88-bundles moves modal_bundle.glyph_crop onto the CDP crate. 36 crop pairs compared, none differing.

decisions.summary: archive.py cut to the reads its importers use plus forwarders for every write and the browser, until S3b and S4 delete it
decisions.why: FR-001 places uncited/uncited_imports/archive_ops in S3b and research_search/semantic_index in S4; half-ported reads with one writer is the ask:449-T81-slices / ask:449-T86-door pattern under FR-003.

decisions.summary: This slice wires the Rust into production callers (Makefile archive recipes, record::reserve in process, depiction.rs's crop, tree's stamp, Python writes forwarded) rather than landing a library with no production caller
decisions.why: ask:449-phase4-slices' default slice shape (library, Python staying the implementation) yields here to the more specific ask:449-T80-order (4), which phase4-slices itself invokes for S3a's order and which moves the Chromium install off the Python package in the same cut, with T145's precedent under ask:449-T88-bundles. It ports more, not less, of what the GM asked ('all be ported to Rust'), and the purpose of the slice shape, one wired implementation (FR-003, FR-001c), holds: each file has one live writer, the Rust, with the 13 importer cases in the differential. Nothing the request or spec asked for is narrowed.

decisions.summary: chromium.pin pins Chrome for Testing headless shell 151.0.7922.34 by SHA-256 (the build Playwright 1.62 installed); install-chromium.sh replaces `playwright install` in setup-dev-env.sh; the Playwright package stays in requirements-dev.in until S7 ports page_lit, page_lit launching the pinned Chromium via executable_path; tree's stamp salts the browser area with the pinned version
decisions.why: ask:449-T80-order (4): 'the Chromium install moved off the Python package in setup-dev-env.sh in the same cut' - the install moves, the package is not required to go; page_lit is S7's (ask:449-phase3-remainder, phase4-slices) and FR-001 places setup-dev-env.sh's Python and requirements in phase 4. The salt keeps cache keys correct.

decisions.summary: The plain GET runs curl, sharing the page context's cookies as Playwright's request context did
decisions.why: Implementation of the port, T145's fetch precedent; the 109-case differential (cookies, redirects, PDFs, binary, 404s) holds the outputs (FR-002).

decisions.summary: Node's words kept for the failures the Python's reports name (refused, not found, timeout, redirect cap); other fetch failures carry curl's own error text
decisions.why: An FR-002 output not held byte for byte, so narrowing. ask:449-T066-json-message is a general ruled case - where a message quotes a library's own error text inside a fixed message, verdict, exit, location and fixed words match and the quoted text is the replacement's - with the spec lint as its instance, not its limit. The plan holds more than the ruling requires (the named failures keep Node's words) and lets only the quoted library text of unnamed failures change. curl is a program rather than a Rust library, but the ruling's purpose - a port cannot reproduce another fetch library's own error strings - applies unchanged. No case in the 109 surfaced such a difference.

decisions.summary: The archive's working copy and manifest rows written by the Rust alone; archive.py's ensure, push, place_gm, archive_url, _lane, settle, sync_gm_copies, write_row, Browser, fetch and wayback forward to door verbs; reads, the lock and Archive's git reads stay Python; a Rust verb run by a Python caller under that lock takes no lock itself
decisions.why: FR-003 and ask:449-T86-door (one implementation writing each file, door verbs, no logic in the door); ask:449-T81-slices allows the reads to stay half-ported. Not re-taking the caller's lock prevents self-deadlock without opening a second writer.

decisions.summary: One seam (Reach, cli_with) replaces store, browser and credential in the crates' tests; one kept end-to-end case in tests/hooks/test-l7r-gate.sh drives record archive url, backfill and gm-copies through the real launcher on the pinned Chromium, a local bare remote, empty secrets and a dead proxy
decisions.why: ask:449-T80-order (4): 'behind one seam, one end-to-end test'; FR-008 exempts the one end-to-end test from the tenth-of-a-second bar; ask:449-T146-browser's 'its one end-to-end test'.

decisions.summary: The production wiring that hands in the real store, browser and credential (cli, production_store, start_browser, token, Process::start) is #[cfg(not(test))], so it is outside the unit-test coverage instrument and reached only by the end-to-end case
decisions.why: FR-004 read strictly asks every line reached by a test; these lines leave the unit-test instrument's denominator, so narrowing. Legitimate on the spec's own words: ask:449-T80-order (4) and ask:449-T146-browser put the browser behind one seam with one end-to-end test, its lines owing FR-004 'with its one end-to-end test', and FR-008 bars any other test from starting the real browser and process. The ruling holds only while the excluded set is the named hand-in of real store, browser, credential and process (cli, production_store, start_browser, token, Process::start); any logic behind cfg(not(test)) beyond that is not covered. Evidence gap: the block's label for 'executes every line of those blocks' (run, and run with no Chromium) shows the case depends on Chromium, not line reach, so line reach is asserted rather than shown.

decisions.summary: make archive-find, dead on AttributeError since T145 cut attempts.report, restored by a forwarder
decisions.why: Restores behavior FR-002 bound T145 to keep; the forwarder reaches the Rust, so FR-003's one implementation holds.

decisions.summary: The Rust archive-sources deadlock (stdout lock held while lanes printed) fixed
decisions.why: A defect in the port itself, fixed so its outputs match the Python's (FR-002).

decisions.summary: S1's entry_bodies read the whole registry per entry; fixed, cited from 8.7 s to 74 ms with the same output
decisions.why: A fix in already-ported Rust that this cut calls, holding the output; it serves the request's stated purpose (the code's inefficiency) and narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: fancy_regex back-references matched case-sensitively where Python ignored case; the pattern spells the cases out
decisions.why: A port defect fixed toward the Python's behavior (FR-002).

decisions.summary: Chromium given its own directory instead of leaving files in TMPDIR
decisions.why: FR-013: the tooling must not leave what it makes on disk.

decisions.summary: HEAD's Python and Playwright against the Rust in network namespaces with recorded pages and a local bare remote, every output and file compared over 109 cases; normalizations limited to values two Python runs differ in (stamps, times, MHTML boundary, Content-IDs, Date, soft breaks, sorted server log, git log as multiset) plus traceback text and argparse text on exit 2
decisions.why: FR-002's comparison; normalizing run-to-run nondeterminism of the Python itself loosens nothing it binds, and traceback and argparse text are excluded by the ruled case ask:449-usage-text. T80-order (4)'s measurement on real sources stands as the replay of recorded real archive pages.

decisions.summary: The one differing case, archive_ops find, is held to the pre-T145 Python (b5a370293^) instead of HEAD's, which crashes on T145's defect
decisions.why: A departure from FR-002's literal baseline (HEAD's Python) with no ask behind it, so narrowing. Literal matching would require the Rust to reproduce an AttributeError crash that T145's own port introduced in breach of FR-002, which defeats FR-002's purpose (the tools keep doing what they did) and the request's (a working Rust tool). The ruling rests on that purpose alone, not on FR-002's refuses-correct-work exception, which speaks of guards and checks and of defects in the replaced Python. The block names the difference and shows the pre-T145 Python and the Rust agreeing on exit, stdout, stderr and attempts written across all four forms.

decisions.summary: The FR-002 case ask:449-T146-browser ruled on for uncited fetch with a blocked page is not taken, its premise (a Playwright crash at HEAD) shown to be a harness error; the lane's output with the blocked page mid-way held by a kept case
decisions.why: Declining a ruled exception and holding the full FR-002 output is the strict reading, not a narrowing.

decisions.summary: Timings (archive pages, a 96 MB page, crops, the installer) recorded and not held
decisions.why: No requirement binds this task to a timing; FR-010 measures at phase ends.

decisions.summary: No measurements.json names archive.py, glyph_crop or playwright; exits make static, rust-test, hooks-test HOOKS_ALL=1 and a gated land; ordered after S2 (T145)
decisions.why: FR-001's rewrite of recorded measurements in the porting commit; ask:449-phase4-slices' slice order; FR-004 coverage held by make static.

decisions.summary: make decide's lint (asked by make plan-delta too) refuses a sentence stating a count of a measured noun with no label in that sentence, as feature 430 D5 already refuses an unlabeled figure with a physical unit; the message names the labels and says to re-read the count from the run's record after the last edit.
decisions.why: This is the GM's first proposal of 2026-11-16, 'a pre-review figure check in make decide', approved with 'Sounds good, please proceed with that'. It extends D5's existing pre-review refusal to the unlabeled counts that were costing review rounds, which is the evidence the GM was shown.

decisions.summary: Counts of the plan's own parts ('14 decisions', 'two tasks', '11 recipes') are not refused.
decisions.why: These name the document. They make no measured claim about the world, so they are not figures in the project's figure contract. A figure check that refused them would add rewrites, the opposite of the request's purpose of fewer round trips. No measured figure is exempted.

decisions.summary: A rule's threshold ('no file over 1,000 lines', 'at most 10 keys') is exempt.
decisions.why: A threshold states a limit and has no measurement to label, so a label cannot be asked of it. That puts it outside the class of thing the figure check exists for. It narrows nothing the GM asked to have checked.

decisions.summary: Dates, task and requirement ids, and code spans are not figures.
decisions.why: This is the same reading D5's unit check already makes. It is not a new carve-out.

decisions.summary: A count's label is looked for in its sentence only, where the unit check also splits at ';'. The choice was measured over sixteen reviewed sections of 449: 11 flags with the ';' split, 3 with the sentence split, each of the 3 a real unlabeled count.
decisions.why: D5 itself defines the rule at sentence level ('whose sentence carries no label'). The GM's words leave the granularity open, and the plan chose it by measurement, against false refusals that would themselves cost round trips. Nothing the GM asked to have checked is dropped.

decisions.summary: The miscounted-figure case (T145's third return) is answered by the lint's message and by a brief rule (re-measure each figure after the agent's last edit, with its method), not by the lint verifying values.
decisions.why: The GM was shown returns lost to 'unlabeled or miscounted figures' and approved 'a pre-review figure check'. The check reaches the unlabeled case only. Mechanically verifying a one-shot count's value is impossible: its method is an observation or a scratch script that the lint cannot rerun. Keyed figures are already rerun by make figures under the existing contract. The plan does not drop the case: it puts it in the refusal message and in every brief. This is the physical-impossibility ground, not convenience.

decisions.summary: T145's '(183, 98 and 57 lines)' is refused and its labeled form passes, pinned by the lint's tests.
decisions.why: Enforcement of the requested check, on the case that motivated it.

decisions.summary: The GM's second proposal (differentials rerun only the cases a fix touched) is carried 'outside the code', as a rule in every port task's brief from T147 on: each harness keys its cases by inputs and code and reruns only the changed ones, with the full run kept once at the end. The only check is item 9, a one-time look at T147's report. No tooling makes a harness do it or refuses one that does not.
decisions.why: The GM approved 'the differentials rerunning only what a fix touched' (2026-11-16). Earlier, on the exact pattern of port agents rerunning slow checks while iterating, the GM said: 'we need not only for our standard procedures to be running things in a sensible way, our tooling must enforce this, or else future Claude Code sessions, or even this session itself, as the session moves on, will drift back to running extraordinarily slow commands over and over again when faster commands would do' (2026-11-11, request.md). A brief is a standard procedure, and the plan labels this rule 'outside the code'. Nothing keeps it after T147: a brief that omits it, or a harness that ignores it, passes every gate. No GM words confine the 2026-11-11 passage to compiling. It was said after measuring that 'a port agent ran the slow checks over and over while iterating', and a differential is such a check. It is not impossible: a shared case-keyed runner, or a check that refuses a harness without one, is tooling the plan could carry. 'Harnesses are written per task' is cost, not impossibility. To clear: carry proposal 2 in tooling that makes rerunning only the touched cases the default, or that refuses a harness that does not do it, with tests. Otherwise put the brief-only form to the GM or the round arbiter as an exception.

decisions.summary: The third proposal, compile and test speed, is filed as T160, ordered last and opening with a measurement of where compile and test time goes.
decisions.why: The GM was shown it ranked last ('compile and test speed last') and approved the order as shown. Measuring first follows this feature's standing rule for efficiency work.

decisions.summary: T159 lands after T146 and before T147, whose plan it checks first.
decisions.why: The GM: 'Those all seem like goofd things to prioritize so that we can make progress more quickly.' Landing it before the next port honors that.

decisions.summary: Green: the plan crate's tests, full line coverage and make land. Done is measured by the lint's tests, T147's plan reaching review with no figure returned, and T147's report of its harness's selective rerun.
decisions.why: These verify the requested behavior and are within the request. (The weakness of the T147 check as the only hold on proposal 2 is ruled on in T159-proposal2-in-briefs.)

decisions.summary: One shared differential runner, l7r-gate diff-run in a new Rust gate crate, used by every port task's comparison from T147 on in place of hand-written driver loops
decisions.why: It is the GM's approved second proposal of 2026-11-16 ('the differentials rerunning only what a fix touched' ... 'please proceed with that'); Rust is FR-001's rule for new tooling, and it carries FR-002's comparison rather than changing it.

decisions.summary: Case shape: per-side world built by a setup command into a fresh directory, both sides as command templates, per-case steps, outputs compared (exit, stdout, stderr, every file written under the world, named extra files), one results row a case
decisions.why: Takes the shape the T143-T146 harnesses share, so no case is lost moving onto it; the outputs compared are at least what FR-002 binds (verdicts and outputs).

decisions.summary: Named normalizations (regex and replacement), each listed in the report as taken
decisions.why: The runner provides and reports the facility; it pre-authorizes no particular normalization, so FR-002's binding of outputs is not relaxed by this block - each normalization a port uses still answers to FR-002 and its ruled cases, and is visible in the report.

decisions.summary: The old side's result is kept on a key over the case definition, its normalizations, declared inputs and the old side's fingerprint (its files, the Python tree at its revision), so a port fix never reruns it
decisions.why: The old Python does not change under a port fix (FR-003 keeps it as is until replaced); any change to what it runs from moves its key. Rerunning it would only repeat a result the key proves unchanged - exactly the 'rerunning only what a fix touched' the GM approved.

decisions.summary: The new side's key uses the content of the source paths a case declares it exercises instead of the whole binary (whole new-side fingerprint when none declared), so an incremental run can keep a new-side result on a hand-written declaration
decisions.why: On the incremental path a kept new-side result rests on a declaration that can be too narrow, which is less than FR-002's 'every case'. Legitimate because it is the GM's own words ('rerunning only what a fix touched', 2026-11-16) and because the block itself preserves FR-002's purpose: the figures a plan reports come from --verify, one run of every case's new side against the kept old sides, named in the report as a verify run. The ruling rests on that sentence; the lint as described checks only that a diff-run report is cited, not that it is a verify run, so verify-backing is a stated rule rather than a tool-enforced one (noted, not blocking: the block does not relax FR-002).

decisions.summary: --verify reruns every case's new side at the end and is the source of a plan's reported figures; --only <name> reruns one case
decisions.why: --verify is what keeps FR-002's every-case proof under incremental reruns; --only is a narrower rerun, the direction the GM's 2026-11-11 words ask for.

decisions.summary: --twice runs the old side twice and reports what differs, as evidence a normalization covers only run-to-run noise
decisions.why: Moves into the runner a check T146's harness already did by hand; it bounds normalizations, serving FR-002, and adds no behavior the request lacks.

decisions.summary: Incremental rerun is the runner's default
decisions.why: The GM 2026-11-11: 'our tooling must enforce this' so sessions do not drift back to the slowest command; the default is that enforcement.

decisions.summary: --all (every side of every case) takes REASON= of two words or more, recorded in the report and the guard log, as FR-011's escapes do
decisions.why: Same escape shape FR-011 already gives make rust-test and make static; it enforces the requested incremental default and does not forbid the full run.

decisions.summary: make decide's lint refuses a sentence stating a differential's case count (cases beside 'differential' or FR-002's 'same outputs') that cites no diff-run runner report
decisions.why: Enforcement of the requested thing - port differentials going through the runner that reruns only what a fix touched - as the GM's 2026-11-11 rule asks ('our tooling must enforce this'). Note: it is a refusing guard and the block does not bound which features or tasks make decide applies it to; the GM's enforcement rule is not feature-limited, so not ruled out of scope, but its reach is worth stating in the plan.

decisions.summary: What a world needs beyond a setup command (network namespace, loopback server, bare remote) stays the harness's setup script, which the runner runs and keys
decisions.why: No class of case escapes the runner: the setup script is still run by it and is part of the key, so such cases still rerun only when touched. Only native modelling of those worlds is left out, which the request never asked for.

decisions.summary: Order after T159 and before T147 (its first user); exits: the crate's tests and coverage including named rerun/keep/verify/--all/lint cases, make land green; done measured by T147's runner reports counting reruns and kept sides, figures from a verify run
decisions.why: Order follows the GM's ranked list (figure check first, then the differentials); FR-004 coverage held; the exit tests check the requested behavior.

decisions.summary: Classed 'Performance work? No' - it saves an agent's waiting on reruns, not the tools' running time
decisions.why: The task is filed under the GM's direct approval of 2026-11-16, not the 2026-11-12 conditional pre-approval, so that pre-approval's measured-target condition does not govern it; it still carries a dated, methoded measurement of the wait it targets. The classification narrows nothing the GM asked for.

decisions.summary: uncited.py, uncited_imports.py and archive_ops.py ported (new gate crate `uncited`, archive operations into the `archive` crate) and deleted; attempts.py and reserve-prefix.py, imported by no Python any more, deleted
decisions.why: FR-001 and ask:449-phase4-slices S3b / ask:449-T80-order (3) place exactly this cluster; deleting a ported file is the GM's standing approval (FR-001, 2026-11-10).

decisions.summary: make uncited, cite-uncited, archive-sources, archive-inbox, archive-find, downloads ingest, record sources outcome cited: and uncited install wired to the Rust in this cut, Python by-path runs retired
decisions.why: Departs from the letter of ask:449-phase4-slices ('a slice lands its Rust as a library with no production caller'), but toward the request (the GM 2026-11-15: port until all tooling is ported) and not against that rule's purpose: the callers are make targets and Rust crates, no Python importer of these files remains, and Python stays the implementation for S4's importers. It does more of what was asked, so it narrows nothing; it does make the task non-straight under FR-001c, which this review covers.

decisions.summary: archive.py and sources.py cut to the names S4's research_search.py and semantic_index.py import (read-only names plus the `push` door); door verbs only the deleted importers used retire
decisions.why: The ask:449-T81-slices test and ask:449-phase4-slices (Python stays for Python importers until wired); doors are deleted with their last caller on the spec's T065 pattern.

decisions.summary: The filter's three lists written by uncited::lists alone; every other write through the one writer S2/S3a gave it
decisions.why: FR-003 as written.

decisions.summary: relayout (no caller) and verify --sample (CPython's Mersenne Twister and random.sample ported so a seed draws the same sample) ported, not dropped
decisions.why: Porting rather than dropping keeps FR-002's same outputs; dropping would have been the narrowing.

decisions.summary: rglob's CPython 3.14 listing order reproduced in archive::ops; research::pyre folds U+0130/U+0131 with i/I under an inline i flag as CPython re.I does, moving only (?i) patterns; archive_urls uses one browser for all its URLs, outputs the same
decisions.why: Each moves the Rust toward the Python's outputs (FR-002); the browser change is an implementation choice with outputs held equal (FR-006's one-process direction). Unmeasured premise noted, not blocking: 'the five in uncited; prepass's one other translates as before' carries no method, and it can only widen what matches CPython.

decisions.summary: T146's kept blocked-page case becomes uncited::fetch's unit test (same words, 120-char cut); tests/hooks/test-l7r-gate.sh runs the Rust production paths on the real browser behind dead proxies
decisions.why: The Python lane it drove is deleted; the case moves to the Rust whole, and the end-to-end test stays the one FR-008 and ask:449-T146-browser allow.

decisions.summary: Differential normalizations taken under ruled cases: the JSON parser's words in install's refusal, argparse's usage/error text (also before make's line), uncaught traceback text
decisions.why: Each is a case FR-002 itself rules apart (ask:449-T066-json-message; ask:449-usage-text, including tracebacks). The patterns in cases.json replace only the library/argparse/traceback text: exit status, stdout and the fixed words around the JSON message are still compared.

decisions.summary: Stamps, ISO dates, Date headers, MHTML boundaries/cids, tmp paths normalized
decisions.why: Values that differ between two runs of the same Python; comparing them is impossible, not merely awkward.

decisions.summary: Two lanes' appended lines (not-kept.jsonl, source-attempts.jsonl, import-check.jsonl) sorted
decisions.why: Opt-in only on the two --workers 2 cases (fetch, verify --sample 3), where two workers append in either order on the Python side too; the Python's own order is not fixed, so it is not an output FR-002 binds. Premise asserted from the worker design rather than measured by a repeated Python run.

decisions.summary: T146's sorts: sorted-stdout, server-log-sorted, git-log-sorted
decisions.why: The block names no object or reason; read in the cited cases.json: sorted-stdout is opt-in on exactly the three --workers 2 cases (fetch, verify --sample 3, consulted), whose Python output order is set by worker completion; server-log-sorted sorts the loopback stub server's request log, the world's record and not a tool output, filled by a browser's concurrent requests; git-log-sorted applies to no case (no case captures a '<log ' file). None hides a fixed Python order.

decisions.summary: Incremental rerun counts and timings recorded, timing not held; census of measurements commands; make static/rust-test/hooks-test/pointer check as the checks
decisions.why: FR-001's measurement-rewrite census, FR-004's coverage and the kept checks of FR-001c; timings recorded with date and method, not a bar.

decisions.summary: With no L7R_DISPATCHER, the clone-sync guard reads the session's own process arguments and treats the session it was forked from (--fork-session --resume <parent transcript>) as its dispatcher, letting the forked job through the parent's clone.
decisions.why: A defect fix in a guard this feature ported (constitution XIV), found on this feature's own T147 port agent; it narrows nothing the GM asked (the port of all tooling to Rust) or the spec states, and it reuses the dispatcher exemption the ported guard already has rather than inventing a new rule. Every case the guard's existing tests hold keeps its verdict (FR-002).

decisions.summary: Only a --fork-session resume counts as a launched job; a plain resume stays refused beside a live claimant; the parent id is the resumed argument's leaf less .jsonl.
decisions.why: Bounds the exemption to the measured defect and keeps the guard's existing refusal for every other case; restricts the fix, not the request.

decisions.summary: The exemption is the one a page session already has: the dispatcher's claim alone is let through, every other live claimant still refuses.
decisions.why: Keeps the guard's purpose (two unrelated live sessions never share a clone) intact; nothing the GM asked is narrowed.

decisions.summary: Guard tests green with a forked-through and an unforked-refused test that fails with the fix removed; guard line coverage complete; make land green.
decisions.why: Enforces the fix and holds FR-004's coverage floor; verification of the change itself, not added scope.

decisions.summary: The embedder is ort =2.0.0-rc.10 with tokenizers =0.23.2 over the same Xenova/bge-m3 model_int8.onnx and tokenizer the Python used; fastembed-rs not taken.
decisions.why: ask:449-phase4-slices (spec-cited FR-001) rules that semantic_index 'runs the same BGE-M3 weights in Rust against the stored index'. The same weights file and tokenizer, run against the stored index, is exactly that. Which Rust runtime to use is a choice the ruling leaves open. The block's longer Q11 quote naming fastembed-rs or ort is not in the cited spec text, so the ruling's own sentence is what this rests on.

decisions.summary: The model is read from the mirror's .specify/model-cache/ and never downloaded. With no model present, the tool exits 1 and states the fix.
decisions.why: FR-002 binds outputs 'on every case its tests and its suites hold'. The differential's 174 cases include every refusal, and the block reports none differing. A missing-model run that downloads is not among the held cases the bundle shows. This decision is within only because of that clause. It does not depend on the cache happening to hold the model. If a kept test or suite case does hold the no-model path, it is bound and this becomes a new ask.

decisions.summary: The embedder copies the Python's numerics: fastembed's tokenizer setup, batches of 8, Level3 graph optimization, half the online cores, the CLS row and numpy's pairwise float32 norm.
decisions.why: These choices are how FR-002's identical outputs are reached. The block reports query vectors 68 of 68 and 41 new passage vectors bit-identical, with dated method labels.

decisions.summary: rust/embed (l7r-embed) is a binary of its own, reached through l7r-gate.sh embed serve. No gate or guard crate depends on it, and the make-only guard refuses l7r-embed when run bare. Each point has a test.
decisions.why: This follows the pattern ask:449-T146-browser sets: its own binary, kept out of the guards' and the gate's build path. FR-005 is met by the guard covering the new binary. The browser ruling holds that crate's own lines to FR-004's full coverage and FR-008's test-time bar with one end-to-end test. That pattern binds rust/embed the same way, and this clearance rests on it. The block states 'no exemption taken'.

decisions.summary: The claims walk prunes embed.
decisions.why: Nothing in request.md, spec-cited.md or spec-index.md binds the claims walk's reach. A grep for 'claims walk', 'walk' and 'prune' finds nothing on it. The prune is a consequence of keeping the binary outside the gate's build and takes nothing the GM or the spec asked for. This rests only on that negative search. The browser amendment as cited says nothing about the claims walk, so 'like the browser' does not by itself carry the prune.

decisions.summary: Microsoft's ONNX Runtime 1.31.1 release, the version the Python wheel shipped, is pinned by SHA-256 in scripts/container/onnxruntime.pin, installed by install-onnxruntime.sh into ~/.cache/l7r-onnxruntime/, and loaded at run time. setup-dev-env.sh runs the install. ort's build-time download (1.22) and the wheel's copy are not taken, and make rust-test does not need the library.
decisions.why: This is infrastructure for running the same model in Rust. It keeps the runtime version the Python used, which serves FR-002. It removes nothing the request or spec asks to keep.

decisions.summary: ONNX Runtime's telemetry, on by default in the Linux build and writing $TMPDIR/.ses, is turned off. HEAD's Python had it on.
decisions.why: The .ses file is a side effect, not a verdict or output FR-002 binds. Turning it off agrees with FR-013, under which the tooling must not leave what it makes on disk. It narrows nothing that was asked.

decisions.summary: make semantic-index, semantic-find and research-search run the Rust (l7r-gate.sh record semantic build|find, record search) with their arguments unchanged, and the Python is deleted in the same cut.
decisions.why: ask:449-phase4-slices says a slice lands its Rust as a library with no production caller, its Python staying the implementation for Python importers until S11 or S12 wires the Rust in. That sentence protects Python importers. The block's census reports that no Makefile, shell, Python, agent file or doc names the four deleted files in command, import or -m form after the cut, so no Python importer is left to protect. Wiring the Rust in and deleting the Python at once satisfies FR-003 (no piece runs both) and FR-001. It does more of the request, not less, and the same ruling's S4 sentence has semantic_index 'run ... in Rust'.

decisions.summary: archive.py and sources.py lose their last importers and are deleted, the archive's last door push retires, and requirements-semantic.* and setup-dev-env.sh's fastembed line are removed.
decisions.why: FR-001 places every requirements*.txt and setup-dev-env.sh's Python in phase 4, and this is phase 4's S4. ask:449-T80-order kept archive.py alive only for research_search.py and semantic_index.py. The GM's standing approval of 2026-11-10 ('Yes please delete Python files once their Rust ports land') covers the deletions. One limit on the evidence: the census greps the four deleted file names, not importers of what requirements-semantic installs. That changes no class.

decisions.summary: Tied hits are compared as their tie group. Copies in the same group may differ in which one is printed: 191 lines in 31 cases. At find --k -3, 836 positions change order, with the largest HEAD gap 5.96e-8. A test pins the index-order tie break.
decisions.why: This applies FR-002's ruled case ask:449-T138-ties exactly. Which copy of an identical group is printed is not bound. Order at negative K may change below a 1e-7 gap, and 5.96e-8 is below it. Sources, spans, fingerprints, similarities, the set of hits, exit status and order at default and positive K are reported unchanged.

decisions.summary: Normalization: argparse's generated text.
decisions.why: FR-002's ruled case ask:449-usage-text: argparse's generated stderr text is not bound, while exit 2 and empty stdout are.

decisions.summary: Normalization: one Python traceback (the empty-shard crash), with its kind and exit status kept.
decisions.why: ask:449-usage-text: 'an uncaught Python traceback's text is not bound for any port, its exit status and stdout staying held'. The block keeps the exit status.

decisions.summary: Normalization: the runner's world path.
decisions.why: No ruling is cited for this one. It is within only if it is the per-side scratch path the shared diff-run harness gives each side, not text the two tools print differently. The block's wording ('the runner's world path') names the harness, and it is read that way here. A path that the Python itself wrote and the Rust writes differently would stay bound.

decisions.summary: Timing and memory are recorded and not held: the verify run took 2,415.8 s, find ran 266.5 s against 251.3 s, search 323.5 s against 324.6 s, builds 59.9 s against 50.4 s, and peak memory was 1,516 MB against 1,252 MB.
decisions.why: No requirement holds a per-task time or memory bound on this port. FR-010 and SC-003 measure at phase end and over the suites. Every figure carries a dated one-shot method label.

decisions.summary: Shard zip times remain the write time, as the Python's were. The untracked rust/Cargo.lock leaves transitive versions floating, with ort and tokenizers pinned exactly.
decisions.why: The first keeps the Python's behavior. The second keeps the workspace's existing state, and the crates the embedder's outputs depend on are pinned. Neither narrows anything asked.

decisions.summary: One kept case in tests/hooks/test-l7r-gate.sh runs the real model through the production make paths, holding a vector bit for bit against the Python's, behind dead proxies.
decisions.why: This is FR-008's one end-to-end test against the real command. It enforces FR-002's identical output, the thing that was asked.

decisions.summary: Port the record site's build and checks (site, site_pages, site_links, money, citations, glossary_source, record_asset, glossary_asset, footnote_census, source_tags_contract, memo_check) into the research crate, wire them, delete fifteen Python files, cut record_build.py to a forwarder for render_cache.py and glossary.py to the GLOSSARY/CASED page.py reads.
decisions.why: This is S5 of ask:449-phase4-slices, with T140's files (ask:449-phase3-remainder) folded in as that ruling says. It is wired before S11/S12 rather than landed as a library alone, but that moves toward FR-001 rather than narrowing it. The forwarder and the trimmed glossary.py keep one implementation running for the Python importers that are left (FR-003), and because the slice is wired it keeps its review under FR-001c's 'one wired implementation' reading, which is what is happening here.

decisions.summary: make record / glossary / footnote-census / source-tags-contract and their CHECK=1 forms run l7r-gate record verbs; the push's record and glossary rows run in process and still write the usage-log row; render-sync reaches record site-stale through the forwarder; the four retired rows leave _invocation.py's operations and their make-only suite cases move to a recipe that is still wrapped.
decisions.why: Moves each caller onto the port in the cut that deletes the Python (FR-003). make stays the entry point and the make-only coverage is kept (FR-005). No caller is dropped.

decisions.summary: memo_check's general form is ported beside its presets, with the same output, exit, kept pass, memo path and shape and usage-log row. Its key hashes the program id plus the --code files and their project modules, where the Python hashed its interpreter, so one kept pass is missed once after the cut. The usage line names the port.
decisions.why: Every bound output is held. The key's content is internal, and the only effect is one extra re-run with the same verdict. Once the Python is deleted, a key that hashes the Python interpreter cannot be reproduced. Naming the tool in the usage line is ask:449-T135-generator: the message names its generator and the same cut deletes that generator.

decisions.summary: The record check's memo key is the Python's, with no date in it. The date the port first added is removed after the plan review, and the Python's kept-pass-outlives-the-pending-window behavior is reported to the GM separately rather than changed.
decisions.why: This holds FR-002 exactly. Making a check refuse more is not the fix exception, which covers a check that refuses correct work, so keeping the Python's behavior and raising the issue apart is the faithful choice.

decisions.summary: KeyError str(e) matches (store.py reads e.args[0], as store.rs does). An uncaught exception's line adds Python's repr quotes, pinned by a test. The guard's shared::url_host ports urlsplit exactly and matches CPython 3.14.4 on 3,844 URLs regenerated from HEAD's blocked.host. unicode-normalization is added, and the guard's cold build goes from 23.4 s to 27.0 s.
decisions.why: blocked.py is deleted in this cut, so the Rust host reading is now the one implementation and FR-002 needs its outputs to equal HEAD's. The traceback text is not bound (ask:449-usage-text), and matching it anyway costs nothing. The build-time cost is not a fidelity matter.

decisions.summary: site_pages.py::frame, a no-research claim on process plumbing, leaves dev/claims-index.json instead of being re-keyed, because its code moves into a gate crate the claims walk prunes. The two deleted units leave dev/claims-deferred.json, and make claims-owed owes none afterwards (ask:449-T148-claims).
decisions.why: ask:449-phase4-slices says claims keyed to deleted .py units are re-keyed by claims carry, and that a claim carry cannot map is a new ask. This is that case, and the ask was raised. The rule exists so that no claim stays keyed to a deleted unit and no research claim loses its anchor. Re-keying cannot be done here because the claims walk has no unit to key to in a pruned crate. The claim says no research is needed, so dropping it loses no research link, and the rule's own end, 'lands no claim keyed to a deleted unit', is met. The ask's own text is not in the bundle. This ruling rests on the spec's provision for such an ask and on the plan's account of it.

decisions.summary: S1's record library is made faster with no output changed: a hand-written linkify scan, patterns compiled once, an index on Catalog. The byte-equal site is the evidence.
decisions.why: Output stays byte for byte (FR-002). Speed is the purpose the GM gave for the port ('our Python code is just to inefficient').

decisions.summary: The differential's one difference is render-sync's research/site/.stamp. It hashed the Python modules the build imported, which this cut deletes, and it now hashes the building binary, as the ruled generator-cache key does. Every page and the rebuilt/fresh verdicts are the same.
decisions.why: This is an output difference that no FR-002 ruled case names. Reproducing it literally cannot be done: the modules it hashed are deleted in the cut. Hashing them anyway would defeat the stamp's purpose, which is to mark the site stale when the code that builds it changes, because the stamp would then follow code that no longer runs. Its verdicts, the only thing a reader takes from it, are held. It follows the key ask:449-phase4-slices already rules for gencache (the binary's hash).

decisions.summary: The differential normalizes UTC times and the runner's world path, argparse and traceback text, and the tool's own name in the usage line. The push's two side-by-side rows may append their usage lines in either order.
decisions.why: Times and paths differ between two Python runs. argparse and traceback text are unbound under ask:449-usage-text, and the tool name follows ask:449-T135-generator. The rows run side by side, so the order of their concurrent appends is not fixed in the Python's run either. If the Python's push ran them one after the other, that order would become a bound difference.

decisions.summary: Timings are recorded and not held. The measurements census finds no command that runs a deleted tool. make static, rust-test, hooks-test HOOKS_ALL=1, quick and the pointer check are clean.
decisions.why: These are the FR-001 measurement-rewrite census and the standard exits. Nothing is narrowed.

decisions.summary: Fix a defect T148 found in the record check (make record CHECK=1): its kept pass is keyed on inputs and program but its refusals read today's date (a pending-upload archive row answers for seven days), so a pass kept one day is replayed past a row's window; the key now holds today's UTC date (rust/gate/crates/research/src/tools/memo.rs), in its own commit after T148's port.
decisions.why: Nothing the GM asked is narrowed, and FR-002 does not reach the change: FR-002 binds a replacement's verdicts to the Python's on every case its tests and its suites hold, and the case changed here - a pass kept on one day replayed on a later one past a pending row's seven-day window - is held by none of them (the plan adds the first test of it, failing without the fix); every fresh run's verdict is unchanged. The change is also kept out of the port itself: T148's port kept the Python's key under FR-002, and this lands in its own later commit, so FR-002's one fix exception (a check refusing correct work) is not stretched to cover a check made to refuse more. The plan cites constitution XIV (a defect fixed where it is found), whose text is not in the bundle; the defect - a check passing work it would refuse when run - is in the tooling the request ports, and fixing it narrows nothing asked.

decisions.summary: The glossary check's memo key, which reads no date, is left unchanged.
decisions.why: The defect is a date-dependent refusal replayed across days; a check that reads no date cannot have it, so leaving its key alone drops nothing the request or spec asks for.

decisions.summary: Accept that the kept pass is rerun once a day (fresh 2.2 s vs kept 0.06 s, observed 2026-11-16, /usr/bin/time, T148).
decisions.why: A once-a-day 2.2 s rerun is the cost of the check being correct; it does not undo any of FR-011/FR-012's named savings and no requirement binds the record check's memo hit rate.

decisions.summary: Verify with a research crate test that a pass kept on one day is not replayed the next, shown failing without the fix, plus make static and make land green.
decisions.why: A test whose only effect is to hold the fix in place is enforcement of the work, not added scope.

decisions.summary: Order right after T148; red exit records the failure and routes any cannot-be-done claim through make arbiter-ask; budget one landing.
decisions.why: Sequencing and exit procedure decide nothing the request or spec left open in a narrowing direction.

decisions.summary: S6 ports the registries' readers to a new gate crate `registry` and entry_owed to the owed crate; deletes entry_owed.py, open_questions.py, check-entry-headings.py, owed_door.py, record_door.py and record_cache.py.
decisions.why: Exactly ask:449-phase4-slices' S6 ('the registries with entry_owed, the doors owed_door, record_door and record_cache deleted'), with check-entry-headings.py placed with the registry by ask:449-T065-scope, open_questions.py by ask:449-T79-moves and record_cache.py's deletion by ask:449-T81-slices. The request is to replace the Python with Rust; this is that.

decisions.summary: classes/*, compound_kinds/*, conditions.py and choices.py stay frozen and read-only for the Python importers still unported (page.py, sheet.py, buildings/types.py, the pool generators, render_cache.py), while the Rust readers use kinds.rs; a test of the real tree holds kinds.rs equal to the Python classes by name, key and order.
decisions.why: ask:449-phase4-slices has a slice's Python stay the implementation for Python importers until S11/S12, with an edit of the Python under it mirrored in the Rust in the same commit; ask:449-T81-slices' read-only test is the established pattern. Each reader runs one implementation (FR-003). The equality test enforces the mirroring for kinds.rs; conditions and choices rest on being frozen, which the request's own 'we are no longer changing it' supports.

decisions.summary: The modal prose is not moved: it stays in l7r/diagram/interactive/assets/modals/{hamlet,sheet}/<slug>.md (feature 319), rather than 'beside the Rust registry' as ask:449-phase4-slices words it; the old-to-new id map is recorded and measured empty.
decisions.why: Judged in two halves. (a) Out of Python, one Markdown file per kind: measured already true (all 160 kinds' modal_text byte-equal to the file, no class docstrings, observed 2026-11-16), so that half of the ruling is met, not narrowed. (b) The location 'beside the Rust registry': not done, and this is the narrowing. Against request.md it leaves no clause unmet - the GM asked for the Python replaced, and both FR-001 censuses count .py files and inline Python, not Markdown; FR-009 keeps the interactive page's assets outside the port, so the files' directory survives the Python's removal. The ruling's FR-002 allowance for changed ids was a license, not a requirement; the empty map (297 modals, uid, class, key, file and three fingerprints unchanged) uses none of it, so FR-002 is held strictly and no round or ruling needs carrying. Scoped to S6: this does not settle where the prose lives at the S13 close.

decisions.summary: The push's two entry-headings rows, make audit's silences, make open-questions, record-owed's entry-drift family, the depiction bundle's knobs, modals.rs and the owed crate's modal classes are switched to the Rust; docs and agent files naming deleted files rewritten; make agent-sync rerun.
decisions.why: Moving every caller in the cut is what FR-003 and the doors' deletion in S6 require; the knobs leaving bundle_door is the phase-4 verb ask:449-T88-bundles placed.

decisions.summary: Where the port first differed it was made to match: the no-engine refusal reads 'ImportError:', and a crash or failed self-test of the headings check records no usage row.
decisions.why: FR-002: same outputs as the Python.

decisions.summary: The 42 claims on these units sit in files that stay; none is keyed to a deleted unit; claims-owed owes none.
decisions.why: ask:449-phase4-slices requires a cut to land no claim keyed to a deleted unit; measured that none is.

decisions.summary: Differential normalizes UTC times and the world's base commit and path.
decisions.why: Run-dependent values, not outputs a port could hold equal; FR-002 binds the rest.

decisions.summary: Differential normalizes argparse's and a traceback's text.

decisions.why: FR-008, met and measured.

The block does not show them over the bar at HEAD: this ruling does not cover a slowdown this task caused (it changes what the owed crate's modal classes read), which would be this task's FR-008 debt, not a separate task's.

decisions.summary: Timings recorded, not held.

decisions.summary: Measurement census (no measurements.json runs a deleted file), the gate checks, order after T148 and T163, exits and budget.

decisions.why: A defect fix under constitution XIV in an already-ported Rust check: it narrows nothing and widens the check only to the entries it was meant to cover. Every existing line stays byte for byte (cmp-proven with the sheet additions removed), so FR-002's held outputs are kept, and FR-004's coverage is kept by the new tests.

decisions.summary: a_bare_world_compares_everything_under_it now runs a step with no clock stamp in its output, so the two sides no longer differ across a second boundary.
decisions.why: A test fix that keeps what the test compares. It changes no tool output or verdict.

decisions.summary: Twelve tests over FR-008's bar are split, each keeping every assertion, on a shared fixture with fewer git calls; one test moves to tests/answer_modes.rs; production changes (answer() reusing units, fixed_answer() asking git once, triage writing each page once) change no output.
decisions.why: Carries out FR-008 for the owed crate. No assertion is dropped, and the production changes are held to identical outputs per FR-002.

decisions.id: T164-4 workspace debt deferred to T160
decisions.summary: 159 of 2,354 workspace tests run over the bar, and a temporary directory under the crowded /tmp costs about 20 ms; both are measured and assigned to T160 (compile and test speed), not fixed here.
