decisions.summary: make static, make rust-test, make hooks-test HOOKS_ALL=1 and make land green; a claim that it cannot be done is ruled through make arbiter-ask.
decisions.why: The standing gates. They decide nothing that the spec leaves open.

decisions.summary: The stale-figure check reads a Rust const or static (impl ones included) whose own doc holds Research: and whose value or doc changed since the merge base; base literals normalized as Python writes them, 0 and 1 skipped as the Python skips them; Python path unchanged.
decisions.why: This is the first of the two pieces the GM was told would be made to work on Rust units before S7 and answered 'sounds good'. The reading follows the Python's own rules, and the demonstration (BEND_WIDTHS 2.5 to 3.0 names the stale page) shows it does what it is for.

decisions.summary: Counter-only clear on Rust: a counter statement is a cfg(feature=counters) block or statement (gated if/for refused) or a tally/merge/counts.add call keyed kind@function whose value uses only numbers, places, .len(), integer casts, *, + and parentheses; 79 of 98 call sites fit, the other 19 owe a check as before.
decisions.why: The second piece the GM approved. A counter-only clear is by its nature confined to statements that cannot change behavior; the form is the definition of 'counter-only', not a carve-out. The 19 call sites that miss it are not cleared, so they owe a check exactly as they do today; nothing goes untracked, which is the purpose the GM stated ('otherwise we'll be porting code without being able to track the claims in the new Rust').

decisions.summary: A Rust unit's claim bundle carries the context a Python unit's does (callees up to six, constants read, two call levels for a distance claim, the CANNOT-TELL chase), names resolved through items and use lines.
decisions.why: Not one of the two named pieces, but it is the 'equivalent Rust tool' the GM asked about: a claim on Rust that is judged with less context than one on Python is tracked less well. It widens rather than narrows, and serves the request's stated purpose.

decisions.summary: Merge-base read lists rust/ paths; the push's claims gate judges rust/ paths (a rust/phases-only delta no longer pushes with owed claims unchecked); tunables --inline reads every crate the claims walk reads.
decisions.why: Each is a place where claims on Rust were not tracked at all; fixing them is what makes 'track the claims in the new Rust' true. The push gate's added refusals are confined to owed claims on Rust units, the exact thing the GM asked to have tracked.

decisions.summary: The claims walk reads every crate under rust/ but target, parked, guard, gate, browser and embed (a new crate walked with nothing declared, held by a test), so an engine slice's Rust lands in its own crate beside rust/phases, never under rust/gate/.
decisions.why: It ensures the ported engine is inside the claims walk, which is the request's purpose. The excluded crates are tooling, not the map engine the GM named; nothing the GM asked to have tracked is left outside.

decisions.summary: Claim carry from a deleted .py unit onto its Rust port (fingerprints never shared) and a Rust unit's fingerprint not holding the constants it reads are left for T166, both fixed before any engine slice.
decisions.why: The GM approved the two named pieces in a task before S7; these two further gaps were found by measurement and are scheduled before any engine slice, so the request's timing ('before the porting of the actual map engine') still holds for them. Nothing the GM approved for T165 is moved out of it. The ruling depends on T166 landing before S7, as the block commits.

decisions.summary: Python units' outputs unchanged through the shared runner (9 cases, none differing); the Rust cases differ only in the lines this task adds, each named.
decisions.why: FR-002 held as written for the Python path; the Rust differences are the requested new behavior.

decisions.summary: make static, rust-test, hooks-test HOOKS_ALL=1, claims-owed, claims-report, pointer check; red exit through make arbiter-ask.
decisions.why: Verification and exits for the requested behavior; no scope change.

decisions.summary: One shared committed port map, dev/claims-ports.json, each entry naming the slice that wrote it; claims rekey (run by make land) reads it; the push's claims gate refuses a claimed .py unit deleted with no move and no map entry.
decisions.why: Serves the GM's 2026-11-17 words directly: 'otherwise well be porting code without being able to track the claims in the new Rust'. A shared map at a fixed path is a design choice; the new refusal only enforces that no claim is lost on a port.

decisions.summary: A mapped, deleted unit's row is re-keyed onto the same label of its Rust unit when that unit carries the claim's text, keeps verdict, note and pages with the old key under 'ported', and is owed a full 'ported' check (never a triage or counter clear); the deferred list re-keyed with it; a row whose text no Rust unit holds is left with its fix.
decisions.why: Carries the claim into the Rust and owes a full check of the new code, which is what the request's purpose needs. Nothing is cleared without a check. The quoted Q10 wording ('re-keyed there with claims carry', 'That cut's landing runs the claims check') was not in the bundle; judged against request.md alone, it is within. Demo log (demo-port.log) shows the three rows carried and owed 'ported'.

decisions.summary: A no-research claim ported into a pruned tooling crate is dropped; one citing research is refused as a new ask.
decisions.why: Exception-shaped, so ruled. The text of ask:449-T148-claims was not supplied, so the ruling rests on request.md alone. The GM's concern on 2026-11-17 is porting 'the actual map engine' without tracking its claims in the new Rust. This drop reaches only tooling crates already pruned from the claims system and only claims that cite no research, so no engine claim and no research-bearing claim is lost: a research-citing one is escalated rather than dropped. The request's purpose survives intact. If the cited ruling does not in fact prune these crates, this ruling falls with it.

decisions.summary: Demonstrated on a scratch clone: three compound.py units ported to rust/mode_a, gate refused them unported before the map, rekey carried them, a real impl-drift round found them IN-STEP plus one UNCLAIMED literal, then the gate passed.
decisions.why: Evidence, not a scope decision. demo-port.log is consistent with the block's account.

decisions.summary: A Rust unit's code key adds NAME=<value> for each crate constant it reads, keyed by name (a moved constant owes nothing); a check records the read values on its row, so a changed value owes its readers, which closes the relabel shortcut for Rust.
decisions.why: Gives a changed Rust constant the same tracking a Python unit already had, which is 'being able to track the claims in the new Rust'. demo-const.log shows a changed BEND_WIDTHS owing its own claim and its four readers (drawn x2, two sink tests); arc and TANGENT_CAP, listed with recorded reads, do not read BEND_WIDTHS in the scratch course.rs, so the four is the full reader set.

decisions.summary: The 286 rows of the 112 claimed Rust units that read a constant are re-recorded under the new scheme without re-checking, so make claims-owed owes none before and after and make claims-report is identical to HEAD's.
decisions.why: Before T166 these rows were not owed on a constant change either, so recording today's values loses nothing the GM asked for. The counts match measure-reads.log ('every claimed unit reading one 112, rows 286').

decisions.summary: Five rows recorded under an older scheme are left as they were, their code unchanged since.
decisions.why: These rows keep the tracking they had before T166: a change to their own code still owes them. The constant-reader owing is this task's own improvement and is not in the GM's words, so leaving five rows out of it narrows nothing that was asked. Whether any of the five reads a constant was not shown in the bundle.

decisions.summary: A .py unit's reader of a changed Python constant still passes on the relabel shortcut; the engine's Python is ported away by S12, and each port's claims are checked fresh as 'ported'.
decisions.why: The request is about tracking claims in the new Rust. Python units keep exactly today's behavior, which FR-002 favors, and any claim carried into the Rust gets a full check on its port.

decisions.summary: Differentials: Python cases 9, one differing only in the 286 migrated rows its index carries; Rust cases 7, five differing only in the intended new lines (readers owed, unported refusals, rekey line, 'ported').
decisions.why: No verdict is changed beyond the new behavior. The differences are the migrated index data and the intended additions, each named.

decisions.summary: The five end-to-end port tests run 0.064 to 0.076 s each, the fixture writing the repository git init would make.
decisions.why: Each is under FR-008's tenth of a second; test-times-five.log agrees.

decisions.summary: Three stale reversal tripwires were accepted by the round arbiter before the impl-drift round ran.
decisions.why: Process record, not a scope decision.

decisions.summary: Order (after T165, before S7), exits, budget and the closing checks.
decisions.why: Follows the GM's 'port those before the porting of the actual map engine'.

decisions.summary: Measure where an unchanged tree's, an owed edit's and the slowest crates' check and test time goes before choosing targets.
decisions.why: The GM's 2026-11-16 approval of the third proposal (compile and test speed) and his 2026-11-12 condition of a concrete target with a measured saving; measurement first is what both ask.

decisions.summary: The checks runner runs the owed crates' already-built test binaries directly, five at once (a crate whose binaries the build does not name keeps cargo test); code views cached by path and blob id keyed to the l7r-rust binary and skipped for format and dead; dead counts the crate family once a run.
decisions.why: Compile and test speed is exactly what the GM approved. Only owed crates still run, so FR-011's reuse of passed results is kept, not loosened; the cargo test fallback narrows nothing; the cache key (path, blob id, binary) invalidates on any change, so no verdict is skipped.

decisions.summary: Archive, diffrun, browser, bundle, task and tree tests brought down, every assertion kept; the remaining 151 tests over FR-008's bar and the end-to-end-test ruling deferred to T167.
decisions.why: Serves FR-008 and the approved test-speed proposal. No assertion is removed, and FR-008 is not narrowed: the unfinished part is handed to a named task, not excused.

decisions.summary: Flaky tests exposed by side-by-side running fixed at their source (an injectable clock, a stub cleaning its fake /proc entry, an unstamped perf report, fake executables written by install), not by running those crates serially.
decisions.why: Keeps the tests' verdicts trustworthy under the approved side-by-side runner; explicitly refuses the narrowing (serialising the runner) in favour of the fix.

decisions.summary: Two live /tmp leaks closed (the make-only suite's /tmp/mo.out, two tests writing into the real /tmp/l7r-check); the 8,536 older /tmp entries, costing about 20 ms a temp dir, not swept by the tooling.
decisions.why: Closing the leaks enforces FR-013/SC-008. Not extending the sweep removes nothing FR-013 requires: FR-013 asks for no leak and leaves the existing pile out of the tooling, and the GM's one-time 'delete those old entries' (2026-11-11) was carried out under T105; under the 2026-11-12 conditions a target under 2 s is not one this task must take.

decisions.summary: The archive's sync refuses files over GitHub's 100 MB limit before committing them (the Python committed them and every later push failed), pinned by a test that fails with the fix removed.
decisions.why: A defect found during the work, fixed under the standing constitution XIV rule; it narrows no requested behavior, and the verdict that diverges from the Python is a push that could never succeed.

decisions.summary: Not taken: building every crate in one cargo call (measured slower, 81 s, and a second artifact set) and the gate's duplicated Python tests (left to their own design).
decisions.why: The approval and the 2026-11-12 conditions are for targets with a measured saving; dropping one measured to cost time, and leaving one outside this task's subject, narrows nothing the GM asked of T160.

decisions.summary: The five live-tree tests (tree stamp self-test, task research boxes, checks research_pointers, rust_tooling detector, question_size) declared each tool's one end-to-end test, a tool being a check or verb, not a crate.
decisions.why: This takes five tests out from under FR-008's tenth-of-a-second bar, so it narrows what the bar holds. FR-008 itself gives each tool 'its one end-to-end test against the real command', and each of these runs the tool's real behavior over the real repository. Their cost grows with the repository (measured from 269 to 430 ms), so the bar is unreachable for them by construction, not merely awkward. In the plan's list each is the only declared test for its check or verb, so no tool gets two. Ruled on FR-008's own words. The text of ask:449-T167-realtree is not in the bundle and this ruling does not rest on it.

decisions.summary: checks' file_scale live-tree test declared by analogy with the five.
decisions.why: This is the same class as D1: the test reads the whole live tree (the_repository_itself_is_under_the_bar...), and it is the only declared test for the file-scale check. It was 89 ms before and does not appear among the slow rows after, so declaring it gives it room to grow rather than excusing a present overrun. That fits the exemption FR-008 grants.

decisions.summary: land's replay_owing test declared land's end-to-end test because it drives the real python3 the tool runs; land's other tests kept under the bar.
decisions.why: This is a different class from D1: it runs a real external program, not the live tree. It is still literally FR-008's 'end-to-end test against the real command', it is land's only declared test, and the rest of land stays held to the bar.

decisions.summary: The markers already carried by browser crop, rustc, research fetch and ci reworded to the one marker phrase.
decisions.why: The wording is unified and no new test is exempted.

decisions.summary: The guard's the_r6_corpus_replayed kept an ordinary test and brought under the bar by replaying eight commands at a time.
decisions.why: This holds one more test to the bar, which is stricter than FR-008 requires.

decisions.summary: Of 2,579 tests, no ordinary test is over the bar except one at the line (98 to 102 ms), called load noise; declared tests up to 724 ms.
decisions.why: The test at the line gets no marker and stays held to FR-008, so the plan exempts nothing here. This is a status report, not a carve-out. See the citation finding in the return.

decisions.summary: Claims tests write what the bundle and record commands leave instead of running them through the Python runner; three new tests run the real commands on each fixture and assert the same files.
decisions.why: Every assertion is kept, and the three new tests stop the fixtures from going stale. This is the method FR-008's bar calls for.

decisions.summary: Where a subject moved, the production value is asserted separately: recycling tested every third page with 25 asserted, test-build timeouts shortened with production timeouts asserted, stand-ins for real programs with one real run kept per crate.
decisions.why: The assertions are kept and the production values are still pinned. This changes how the tests run, not which cases are asked for.

decisions.summary: Checks runner asks git once and lists files in one call, claims-carry reads its target once, guard sweep start reports launch in place of a 0.3 s sleep, landing fetches once; each output the same.
decisions.why: These serve the GM's 2026-11-12 instruction to prioritize the time the tests and the landing take, and every output stays the same.

decisions.summary: Scratch-sweep tests wait until /proc shows no other holder of their files, fixing a once-in-50 race.
decisions.why: This fixes a flaky test inside the suite the task works on (constitution XIV). It adds no behavior.

decisions.summary: No check is built that refuses a new test over the bar.
decisions.why: FR-008 and SC-003 ask for no per-test enforcement. The GM's 2026-11-11 'our tooling must enforce this' is about which commands the iteration loop runs, which FR-011 carries. Declining to build this narrows nothing that was asked.

decisions.summary: Exits: make static, make rust-test, make hooks-test HOOKS_ALL=1 and make land green; a claim of impossibility goes to make arbiter-ask; budget one landing; after T160.
decisions.why: These are procedure only, and they narrow nothing.

decisions.summary: The pilot piece is building_programs.py with the buildings.types registry parse it reads.
decisions.why: The GM accepted 'the smallest real piece of step 1 ported end to end' (request.md 2026-11-17). Per the block's quotation of engine-plan.md, building_programs is in step 1's row, and ask:449-phase4-slices (amended by ask:449-engine-order) puts the audit first. The bundle carries the engine-plan row only as the block's quotation, so I could not check it here.

decisions.summary: A new crate rust/mode_a (binary l7r-mode-a), run through l7r-gate.sh mode-a and depended on by no gate or guard crate. The make-only guard covers it.
decisions.why: FR-005 keeps make as the one entry point, and the guard covers the binary with a red-on-revert test. Where the crate lives is design, not scope. It matches the browser and embedder pattern ask:449-T146-browser set for heavy binaries.

decisions.summary: make building-programs [CHECK=1] runs the Rust, and building_programs.py is deleted in the cut.
decisions.why: 'End to end' means wired. FR-003 says no piece runs both. The block's quotation of engine-order condition 3 says make targets call the Rust. The GM's standing approval of 2026-11-10 covers deleting ported Python. The block lists no importers of the deleted file and gives no search space. If anything still imports it in process, the cut breaks that importer, which is an implementation matter and not a narrowing.

decisions.summary: buildings/types.py stays for its Python importers. A test holds Python load_types() equal, field by field, to the Rust parse of the real types.json, and turned red on a CLASSES edit.
decisions.why: I rest this on text the bundle carries. FR-003 applies per piece: the Python consumers of types.py (compound*, pool_index and the others) are not yet replaced, so their Python remains the implementation. FR-001's sentence amended by ask:449-engine-order says the audit lands first, wired. The bundle's same-commit lockstep sentence in ask:449-phase4-slices sits under 'Before that amendment', and the current form is engine-order condition 3, which the bundle carries only as the block's own quotation. I could not verify that quotation here. The test only enforces the lockstep rule and adds no scope.

decisions.summary: The differential normalizes a Python traceback's frames and compares its last line exactly.
decisions.why: ask:449-usage-text: an uncaught traceback's text is not bound for any port, and exit status and stdout stay held. Comparing the last line is stricter than the ruling requires.

decisions.summary: The differential normalizes argparse's usage block and program name.
decisions.why: ask:449-usage-text: argparse-generated usage and error text is not bound, and exit 2 with empty stdout stays held. --help is bound only where a kept test or suite case holds it, and FR-001b deleted the Python unit tests. The tool's hand-written messages stay compared.

decisions.summary: A library's own words in a JSON, UTF-8 or regex error are normalized, and the error class is compared.
decisions.why: ask:449-T066-json-message lets the quoted parser or library text be the Rust library's. Its wording is general, so naming check 5 as 'the instance' does not limit it to JSON. The ruling still binds verdict, exit status, location and fixed words. I read the block as normalizing only the library's quoted words, so location and the fixed words are still compared. A normalizer that strips more than that would go beyond the ruling.

decisions.summary: The differential found argparse taking -hx and -help as help, and that was fixed.
decisions.why: The defect was a Python-versus-Rust difference, and the final verify run of all 76 cases shows none differing with no case excluded. So the Rust was changed to match the Python. A port that departed from the Python here would be an FR-002 departure needing its own ruling, and nothing in the block says it did.

decisions.summary: Each of the crate's seven files carries a module-level Research NONE claim, and the 80 units owe one impl-drift round at landing.
decisions.why: This is process the request does not narrow. No claim sat on either Python file, so no claim is dropped.

decisions.summary: The pilot's measure is time and tokens by phase, a phase being one dispatch. The port dispatch's time is split into sub-phases, and the claims round and landing are measured into the Done line.
decisions.why: The GM accepted 'wall time and tokens reported by phase' and asked about time and tokens, compile times and test times. All are reported: per-dispatch tokens, port sub-phase times, cold and incremental build, test and check times. Defining a phase as a dispatch is a reading of 'phase', not a reduction of it. The plan-review dispatch's time is not yet given, but exit 9 commits to a phase table in time and tokens, which the Done line completes.

decisions.summary: Three frictions are listed for the GM's pre-approved process improvements, and none is decided here.
decisions.why: The GM asked for obvious improvements from the pilot. Listing them decides nothing.

decisions.summary: This is the first piece of step 1 and the second follows. The red exit sets the task down, and a cannot-be-done claim goes to make arbiter-ask.
decisions.why: The GM said 'proceed with a second real piece of step one ... stop after those first two'.

decisions.summary: The block does not publish a before/after page of every pool sheet for this piece.
decisions.why: In request.md this duty attaches to 'each engine slice', and it is the session's framing of the GM's concern about 'rendering more and more of the maps'. This task lands one piece of step 1's slices, not a slice. Nothing in the block waives the duty, and a slice can publish it at its own close against the pre-slice commit, so nothing is lost by not publishing per piece. Whoever closes the slice still owes it.

decisions.summary: Incremental, --only and --twice differential runs build sparse checkouts of the paths a case declares (world.checkout, WORKTREE over HEAD); --verify and --all always build whole checkouts, kept apart (.whole.json), so only a whole-world verify can be cited by a plan; a test pins that a too-narrow list passes sparse and differs in verify.
decisions.why: A process improvement under the GM's 2026-11-17 pre-approval ('obvious process improvements that seem like no-brainers'). The one possible downside, a too-narrow path list reading as agreement, is closed by construction: the report a plan may cite is always a whole-checkout verify, with no sparse result standing in it, and a test fails with that rule removed. Nothing the GM asked is narrowed; FR-002/FR-001c's comparison is still made on whole worlds. Figures carry observed-date and method labels.

decisions.summary: make static runs the claims-form check (claims coverage --rust) over every crate the claims walk reads, refusing a unit with no claim and no module-level claim, and a claim pointer broken in an unchanged file; 0.05-0.06 s.
decisions.why: Moves a refusal the push already makes to before landing and widens it to pointers an edit breaks in files it did not touch, which are real defects the edit caused and the changed-files push gate would miss; the tree passes it today and it costs a twentieth of a second. It enforces the claims tracking the GM asked to have on Rust units (2026-11-17, T165) and the pilot's no-brainer fixes; no requested behavior is narrowed and no judgment-call downside is introduced.

decisions.summary: The plan review bundle carries, for each ask:<key> a changed block cites, the arbiter record's date, ruling, why and what verbatim, from the feature's own arbiter log first; a missing key is named.
decisions.why: Gives the plan reviewer the rulings it must check against without reading the repository; adds information, refuses nothing, narrows nothing. Pre-approved no-brainer from the pilot.

decisions.summary: make test-times CRATE=<dir> times each test alone by T99's method; reports only, never refuses.
decisions.why: Serves FR-008 (each test under a tenth of a second) as a measurement tool, and keeping it non-refusing follows the GM's performance rule that time is never a gate. No downside beyond its build.

decisions.summary: notes_census is ported as the second real piece of step 1, wired so that `make notes-census` runs the Rust. The Python and its _invocation.py row are deleted.
decisions.why: The GM (2026-11-17) asked for 'a second real piece of step one' and to stop after two. ask:449-engine-order condition 2 names notes_census among step 1's modules. Condition 3 says the make targets call the Rust once it is wired. Deleting a ported Python file falls under the GM's 2026-11-10 'Yes please delete Python files once their Rust ports land' (FR-001).

decisions.summary: parse.py's SVG parse, tagged.py, PRIVY_FILL and sheet.py's SVG reader come in as Rust with outputs held exactly. The four Python originals stay for their Python importers under the lockstep rule, with a bit-for-bit lockstep test over 6 pool and 22 fixture sheets, each fixture asserted to parse.
decisions.why: This is exactly ask:449-engine-order conditions 2 (held exactly) and 3 (Python audit code still imported in process stays bound by lockstep until step 3). The test enforces that ruling and adds nothing to it. It names three functions in three files. PRIVY_FILL, a constant, is under the lockstep rule but no test names it. Condition 3 requires the rule, not a test, so this is not a narrowing.

decisions.summary: The census's sheet half (sheet_counts, stale_sheet_counts, stale_counts), which only a kept Python test reached, is ported with three commands so the differential can reach it. That test's check (feature 294 B15b) moves into the crate's end-to-end test.
decisions.why: FR-002 holds every case a piece's tests hold before its Python is deleted, and FR-001 sends a surviving test along with its piece. Porting the half rather than dropping it keeps the held case. The commands only verify that requested behavior and are not new behavior (enforcement, GM 2026-09-20).

decisions.summary: The ten claims on parse.py and tagged.py stay keyed to those kept .py units. The Rust copies carry each claim word for word where it is true of the Rust; where it is not, they carry a claim stating what the Rust decides. Other new units carry their module's NONE.
decisions.why: Q10 of ask:449-phase4-slices re-keys only in the cut that deletes the unit, and these units are not deleted. Claims on new Rust units are the ordinary claims process, not a hand rewrite of a carried claim. The block says nothing about claims on notes_census.py, which this cut does delete. Q10 requires that the cut land no claim keyed to a deleted unit. The landing's claims check enforces that, so the silence is noted but does not block.

decisions.summary: Decided here only this: the port reproduces HEAD's wrong entrance-board census line exactly, and the four hamlets' notes are left untouched. The fix is filed as T171.
decisions.why: FR-002 binds the port to the Python's outputs. Its one exception covers a guard or check that refuses correct work, and a wrong census line is not a refusal. This ruling covers only T170's reproduce-and-leave choice. It does not clear T171's fix, its regeneration of the notes or its restoration of the test. decisions.why: This is an implementation detail with outputs unchanged (FR-002). It is the kind of no-brainer improvement the GM pre-approved on 2026-11-17.

decisions.summary: A 105-case differential of HEAD's Python against the Rust found no difference. It normalizes only a traceback's frames (its last line is compared) and a library's JSON/UTF-8 wording.
decisions.why: ask:449-usage-text already releases an uncaught traceback's text, so comparing its last line is stricter than required. ask:449-T066-json-message releases a library's own error text inside a fixed message. Both are standing ruled cases of FR-002, and no case is excluded beyond them.

decisions.summary: The pilot's cost is reported by phase: tokens, wall time, the test loop, differential runs and test times.

decisions.summary: Fix the claims walk's Rust item splitter (units.rs item_end) to read raw string literals (r"..", r#".."#, br#".."#) to their own close, so a unit after a raw pattern is no longer swallowed by the unit before it.
decisions.why: A defect in the claims tooling that surfaced in T170's claims round on the second engine piece. The GM, 2026-11-17 (request.md): 'you can also make any no-brainer fixes and improvements which shake out of that while I'm gone ... if there are real tradeoffs then you should wait for me'. The fix has no tradeoff beyond review work: it only adds keys and narrows spans to the item. It also serves the GM's 2026-11-17 request that claims be tracked on the Rust code ('otherwise well be porting code without being able to track the claims in the new Rust'). Nothing the GM asked for is narrowed.

decisions.summary: A claims-crate test covering statics after a raw literal with inner quotes, a byte raw literal with fewer inner hashes, a raw literal ending in a backslash, a raw identifier and an unclosed raw literal; shown red without the fix and green with it.
decisions.why: Enforcement of the fix itself: with the fix removed, the test has nothing left to check.

decisions.summary: The fix's claims round runs in this task as one impl-drift bundle: 32 new claims and 18 reshaped claims in T170's rust/mode_a files, owed in full. Nothing landed earlier is re-judged, because make claims-owed shows that no other crate's unit moved.
decisions.why: Not a carve-out. The scope is what the measured owed set holds (one-shot label: observed 2026-11-17, method make claims-owed / make claims-triage), and every reshaped unit's claims are owed in full rather than exempted. A claim re-judged outside that set would have no moved unit to judge.

decisions.summary: Order after T170, a budget of one landing, done when the owed claims are recorded IN-STEP or fixed, red exits recorded or ruled through make arbiter-ask.
decisions.why: The standard landing procedure for a claims round. It narrows nothing that was asked.

Narrows nothing the request or spec asks for.

decisions.summary: JOBS of 0, a non-number or missing value refused with the fix; a JOBS above the owed sides clamped

decisions.summary: A traceback's frames are normalized away.
decisions.why: ask:449-usage-text: an uncaught Python traceback's text is not bound for any port, exit status and stdout held (T77-bad-since is popup_rounds only and is not the carrier here).

decisions.summary: The piece's cost reported by phase: tokens, wall time, rust-test, differential and verify runs, test times.
decisions.why: The GM 2026-11-17: 'then we'll measure how well those went'; and the pilot's terms, wall time and tokens by phase.

FR-003 and FR-005 carry the deletion and make wiring.

decisions.why: Process only; narrows nothing the GM asked.

decisions.why: Enforces ask:449-engine-order condition 3 and FR-002 (verdicts held exactly); it is verification of what was asked, not new scope.

decisions.why: The GM 2026-11-17: 'the resulting maps do NOT need to be bitwise identical'; ask:449-phase4-slices Q7 as amended by ask:449-engine-order: a check's verdict is bound exactly and a written difference from GEOS that keeps the verdicts is accepted, no new ask. Verdicts are held (the differential's 207 cases, none differing) and the test guards the margin.

decisions.summary: Claims on the kept .py units stay keyed to them; each Rust copy carries its claim word for word or a claim stating what the Rust unit decides where a memo, regex range or figure moved; other new units carry NONE; py.rs's module claim widened.
decisions.why: ask:449-phase4-slices Q10 keeps claims keyed to .py units until the cut that deletes them; those units are kept here, and new Rust units owe their own claims. Nothing is re-keyed by hand. The landing's claims check still holds Q10 for the deleted __main__.py.

decisions.summary: The differential: HEAD's make pack-audit against the Rust over 207 cases (pool sheets, fixtures, notes and manifest forms, file refusals, argument forms, directly and through make), none differing; the runner's world-path normalization for each side's own world.
decisions.why: FR-002, same verdicts and outputs before the Python is deleted. The world-path normalization only maps each side's scratch directory; it releases no output.

decisions.summary: A traceback's frames, and an uncaught JSONDecodeError or UnicodeDecodeError message compared by its class, are not compared byte for byte; exit status and stdout stay bound.
decisions.why: It narrows FR-002's 'same outputs' for these crash cases, but exactly by the accepted spec's ruled case ask:449-usage-text ('an uncaught Python traceback's text is not bound for any port, its exit status and stdout staying held'). The decode errors are uncaught, so their messages are part of that traceback text; the frames name Python files this cut stops running, which a Rust port cannot reproduce. FR-002's purpose, the verdicts and outputs a caller acts on, is untouched: exit and stdout are held.

decisions.summary: The usage line both sides print still names python3 -m ...pack_audit, kept as bound output as T170 kept its own.
decisions.why: It keeps more bound, not less, so it narrows nothing the GM asked. Whether FR-002's ask:449-T135-generator case (a message naming a generator the same cut deletes names the port instead) reaches it is a question of spec consistency, not a narrowing.

decisions.summary: The step's page: step 1 draws nothing, and every pool Mode A sheet before step 1 and now is byte-identical, 6 of 6.
decisions.why: The GM 2026-11-17: each engine slice publishes a page of every pool sheet before and after; ask:449-engine-order condition 5.

decisions.why: FR-002 binds the same verdicts and outputs. Its fix exception covers only a check that refuses correct work today, and none of these refuses anything. ask:449-phase4-slices' defects to fix are other, named ones. Reproducing is what FR-002 asks.

decisions.summary: registry.ft, which has no caller, is not ported.
decisions.why: It narrows 'every Python replaced by Rust' by one function, but FR-002 binds verdicts and outputs, and a function with no caller yields none on any case. The lockstep test over every check's records and the whole report, and the 207-case differential with none differing, would show a difference if any path reached it. The Python registry.py stays under lockstep for compound.py, so nothing that runs loses it. The request's purpose, a Rust codebase that behaves as the Python did, is untouched.

decisions.summary: The piece's measure by phase: tokens and minutes per agent, the lockstep's and the other tests' times, an edit cycle's time, the verify runs' times.
decisions.why: The GM 2026-11-17: 'and then we'll measure how well those went'.

decisions.summary: Exits: make static, rust-test, hooks-test HOOKS_ALL=1, quick, the pointer check, the claims round and a gated make land; red recorded and set down, a can't-be-done claim through make arbiter-ask.
decisions.why: The project's standing gate and FR-001c's kept checks; a wired landing keeps its full review (ask:449-engine-order condition 4).

decisions.summary: Label-only under ask:set-down-449-pieces34: no research pass, fetch or new question; a physical rule no page answers is labeled UNRESEARCHED and listed for the GM (three named).
decisions.why: The ruling's item (3) is exactly this: each rule gets the page that attests it 'or an honest CONVENTION, GUESS or UNRESEARCHED label'; item (4) forbids starting a research pass that could change a rule, a verdict or a map, or that spends money, and requires it be listed as an open item. The GM's 2026-11-17 bound ('proceed with the next 2 engine pieces and then we'll measure') and 'tough judgment calls wait for me' are honored. Nothing the request or the ruling asked for is dropped.

decisions.summary: No code moved: every changed Rust line is a doc comment; the seven Python files' ASTs less docstrings/strings byte-identical; each claim mirrored word for word onto the kept Python copy.
decisions.why: The ruling makes T176 label-only and says 'the Python copies' claims matched'; ask:449-phase4-slices Q1 freezes landed slices' Python so any edit makes the same change in the Rust in the same commit, and Q10 keeps claims keyed to .py units until the cut - mirroring onto both copies satisfies both. The AST comparison is enforcement of the label-only scope, not added scope.

decisions.summary: A claim whose code departs from its page says so (DEVIATION, e.g. the notice board's shadow, road wider than its gate, sanctuary-only fence, a fix-text gate width); the departure is recorded, not fixed here. COVERAGE_TOL's words corrected to what its code does; TUB_DOOR_MAX_FT relabeled CONVENTION on both copies per page 0100.
decisions.why: Fixing a departure changes a rule or a check's verdict, which the ruling's items (3)-(4) put outside T176 and the GM's two-piece bound puts outside this sitting; an honest label that says the code departs is the ruling's 'honest label' applied, and DEVIATION is the truthful class for that case. Correcting a claim's wording to the code and relabeling a constant whose page records a convention are the label corrections the ruling orders (as with HIERARCHY and TUB_KINDS).

decisions.summary: Printed messages citing a stale page or a figure no page gives stay as they are (bound output, FR-002) and are listed for the GM.
decisions.why: FR-002 binds a tool's own words byte for byte to the Python's (ask:449-usage-text: a tool's own words stay bound), and the ruling scopes T176 to labels; changing a message is neither. Listing them for the GM keeps the matter in the report the ruling asks for rather than dropping it.

decisions.summary: Scope: all 61 findings make claims-report listed on rust/mode_a after T175 (NONE-module rules, a mislabeled class, one drifted wording), against the ruling's '~40 rules'.
decisions.why: The ruling's goal is that every rule the audit enforces carries a label saying what backs it; '~40' is the arbiter's approximation, and covering every finding of the same report is that instruction carried out, not new behavior. No code, rule or output is added.

decisions.summary: The shared differential runner keeps each worker's world for the run, one per side, and resets it to the side's revision between cases (outside emptied, .git restored from the copy taken at its making, read-tree -u --reset HEAD, clean -ffdx, WORKTREE laid over again, modes restored, setup rerun).
decisions.why: The GM, 2026-11-18: 'those efficiency improvements are worth making next. Please make those, then proceed with continuing the porting', on the standing 2026-11-12 condition of a concrete target with a measured saving (the tests' and landing's time first). Target measured before: the checkout 1.25-1.33 s and removal 0.27-0.30 s of each side, against a 0.1-0.2 s reset. After: 152.4 s to 51.0 s and 376.1 s to 164.5 s. FR-002's bar is kept on the instrument: all 640 kept results byte for byte the fresh worlds' except their time field, and every report row agrees with the earlier verify.

decisions.summary: A fresh world is made instead when the repository's HEAD or refs moved, the checkout's declaration or a GIT_ variable changed, or a reset step fails.
decisions.why: This guards the reuse's correctness, so a reused world never stands in for a revision it does not hold. It narrows nothing the GM asked for.

decisions.summary: Reuse is the default. --fresh-worlds keeps the old way.
decisions.why: A speed-up to the verify runs, which is what the 2026-11-18 request asks for. The old behavior stays reachable. The default rests on equality tests in which dropping any reset step, swapping read-tree for reset --hard, keeping a case's index, ignoring moved refs or losing the index time turns a test red.

decisions.summary: A reset world's file times are not compared with a fresh world's and do differ: untouched files keep the first checkout's time.
decisions.why: A fresh world never fixed file times either, since each checkout stamps its own arbitrary time, so no kept case's verdict can rest on their absolute values. The measured run shows no kept case depends on the relative times the reuse changes: 640 results are byte for byte the fresh worlds'. This is a limit of the speed-up's equality, stated openly. It does not narrow FR-002's requirement that a port's outputs match the Python's. --fresh-worlds remains for any case later found to read file times.

decisions.summary: Sparse worlds stay fresh and are not reused.
decisions.why: The optimisation is simply not applied to one world kind, which keeps that kind's existing behavior. The request names no world kind to be reused, and the measured goal (a third to a half of a port's verify time) is met without them. Nothing the GM asked for is carved out.

decisions.summary: After T176 and before the port continues. One landing, with its sibling.
decisions.why: Matches the 2026-11-18 order: 'make those, then proceed with continuing the porting'.

decisions.summary: Green exit: the equality tests, make static, make rust-test, make hooks-test HOOKS_ALL=1 and a gated make land. Red exit: recorded and set down, with a claim of impossibility ruled through make arbiter-ask. Constraints named: FR-002, FR-008, FR-013.
decisions.why: These are the standing gates, plus the requirements the change touches (the tests' time bar, and temporary worlds removed). The red exit sends any claim of impossibility to the arbiter rather than letting the session rule on its own case.

decisions.summary: The mode_a end-to-end lockstep reuses the kept Python's output from a keep keyed by a sha256 over everything the Python half reads, rerunning the Python only when the key moves; the comparison, assertions and fixtures unchanged.
decisions.why: The GM 2026-11-18 asked for the efficiency improvements to be made before the port continues, and 2026-11-11 said reusing 'the results of tests which have already run so that we don't have to run them again, is exactly what we should be doing'. The Rust output is still compared against the Python's output for identical inputs, so FR-002's bar is untouched, and FR-008's one exempt end-to-end test keeps its place. (The bundle does not quote the pieces-3-and-4 report, so it cannot show whether this item was on its list; the 2026-11-11 words cover it independently.)

decisions.summary: The key covers the whole l7r/ tree except __pycache__, every name and byte of pool/, tests/fixtures/ and legacy-hand-authored-pool/ including renders, the test's temp files with their path placeholdered, every path passed in, the script and stdin, and the interpreter's identity with every installed distribution's version; docs/ and rust/ are not keyed.
decisions.why: The scope comes from a logged run of the Python half's opens and listings, measured rather than assumed, and is wider than what that log showed (renders are keyed even though the run read none). The two exclusions take nothing away. Bytecode is built wholly from the keyed .py sources. docs/ and rust/ are not Python inputs, so a Rust-only edit is exactly the case the request wants skipped. This decision only sets the cache's key; it narrows no requirement.

decisions.summary: An interpreter that cannot name itself keeps nothing; a missing, unreadable or stale keep reruns the Python; the keep is written to a side file and renamed into .git/rust-tests/.
decisions.why: Every doubtful case falls back to today's behavior, rerunning the Python. The keep is one file that is overwritten, not a temp directory left behind, so FR-013 is not touched.

decisions.summary: Mutation tests show the key moves with each input kind and not with bytecode, docs/ or rust/; a stale keep is not read; a Python edit still turns the lockstep red; coverage is 100% with and without a keep.
decisions.why: These tests only enforce that the requested saving does not loosen the lockstep, and they keep FR-004's floor. That is enforcement of the request, not added scope.

decisions.summary: Before and after timings of make rust-test CRATE=rust/mode_a after a Rust-only edit (9.19 s to 6.85 s wall) and after a Python edit (8.0 s), each with a dated method label.
decisions.why: This measures the requested improvement by the same command before and after. The figures carry one-shot labels (date and method), so they are reviewable.

decisions.summary: S7 ports the Mode A page writer (page.py, place, raster, extents, notes, tags, dwellings, sheet.py's page half) into rust/mode_a, wires write_sheet_page to it, ports picture-diff and page-lit (browser half on the one browser crate), deletes the Python with claims carried; worked as part A then part B
decisions.why: ask:449-phase4-slices Q4 (one browser crate, one image crate), Q10 (claims carried in the deleting cut), Q13 (S7 ports what page.py writes today); ask:449-engine-order sets the wired landing and the order after the audit (step 1) and before step 3. The two-agent split is process, not scope.

decisions.summary: the raster renderer is the resvg library pinned =0.46.0 in the Mode A crate, driven as the binary's main drives it, byte-identical to the binary on every render
decisions.why: Exactly ask:449-phase4-slices Q7 as amended by ask:449-engine-order: resvg a library pinned to the binary's version in the Mode A crate alone; the amendment would even accept a differing PNG, and none differs.

decisions.summary: the page picture's JPEG encode moves from PIL to Rust, same quantization tables and sampling, within one color level of PIL's
decisions.why: The picture is a drawn sheet's output; FR-002 and the GM's 2026-11-17 words ('the resulting maps do NOT need to be bitwise identical') hold it to its checks and research claims, not its bytes; Q4 moves PIL to one image crate. Pixels measured within one level, under picture_diff's threshold.

decisions.summary: with no binary to be missing, a page always draws its picture where HEAD warned and drew none when resvg was absent from PATH
decisions.why: The missing-binary case cannot exist once the ruled change (Q7: resvg becomes a library in the Mode A crate) is made; reproducing a warning about an absent dependency that no longer exists is physically impossible, and the difference is implied by the ruling itself. Declared and shown in cases-renderer.json.

decisions.summary: lockstep against live Python in part A (374 cases, 46 refusals, six pool pages, 11 mutations red); after deletion 134 self-contained cases pinned to Python answers captured before deletion, 240 live-tree cases and six pool pages checked by outcome in the end-to-end test
decisions.why: FR-002 binds the outputs before the Python is deleted, which the lockstep and differential do; FR-001b deletes Python tests and holds what remains by kept checks and differentials; FR-008 allows one end-to-end test. Nothing is excluded from the pre-deletion comparison.

decisions.summary: differential of 135 cases, none differing, with normalizations: the picture's data:image/jpeg URI (pixels held by the measure), traceback frames and chained-cause line, a library's decode wording, argparse usage, regen wall time
decisions.why: Each normalization is a ruled case already in FR-002: the picture under the GM's 2026-11-17 maps rule; traceback text and argparse usage under ask:449-usage-text (which releases traceback text entirely - the block compares more than required); library decode wording under ask:449-T066-json-message; wall time is not an output. The id map's PNG and every other byte stay exact.

decisions.summary: the generation cache is told every file the Rust command read, so a moved stylesheet, script, questions or notes file still regenerates its page; recorded lists match HEAD's
decisions.why: Preserves today's cache behavior (FR-002, FR-006); ask:449-phase4-slices Q8 keys gencache on the inputs the run reads.

decisions.summary: picture-diff/page-lit documented path (A, B as PNG or SVG; PAGE= with picture and id map; OUT=<png>) bound exactly; other formats through the image crate =0.25.9, declared not bound: eleven lossless formats read exactly to PIL's pixels, JPEG and lossy WebP by the crate's decoders, page-lit --out JPEG/GIF/WebP by the crate's encoders, every other PIL-read format (TIFF LA, palette TIFF, oversize ICO) refused by name

decisions.summary: Kept as not being a port's exactness standard: reproducibility (same code and seed give the same map; the cache audit; counters that must not change a map), a lossless split's integrity, a file hash naming its content, and a quotation verbatim from its source.
decisions.why: The GM's words carry the qualifier 'as an exactness standard', and his complaint is that 'things must match' what a port replaces. Each item here compares code with itself, or content with its own hash, or a quote with its source. None is agreement between a port and the thing it replaces.

decisions.summary: Past specs, dated records and history are left as written, and so are finished tasks' plan sections as records of what they measured.
decisions.why: This narrows 'remove any references' literally, but the GM's words name what is to change: 'our project guidelines and speckit constitution and whatever else we need to update to clarify this'. That is the guidance a session follows. A finished feature's spec and a dated record are not guidance for a port going forward, so leaving them does not leave a byte standard in force. Rewriting them would also falsify dated records, including the GM's own verbatim words in gm-rulings.md. The purpose (no future port held to bytes) is not touched. Condition: 'past specs' means features that are finished. A live spec still governing work is guidance and falls under T180-sweep.

decisions.summary: The one measure kept exact is the audit checks' verdicts (each check on each sheet, each guard's verdict on each suite case), and a check that refuses correct work is still fixed in its port.
decisions.why: This is the GM's own condition, 'so long as everything works' (2026-11-18), with 'so long as the changes don't violate our research findings' (2026-10-18, the standing rule FR-002 quotes). The checks' verdicts are how this project decides that everything works and that the research claims hold. Keeping them is the GM's condition, not a byte standard.

decisions.summary: rust/mode_a's lockstep tests stay until a harmless difference makes one fail. At that point the test is changed to hold the verdicts and claims (engine-plan.md condition 3 restated: 'a test may show agreement, bytes are not required').
decisions.why: This is live enforcement, not a record, so it cannot rest on T180-records-as-written. It passes the purpose test on its own terms. The GM's purpose is that a port is never stopped, narrowed or sent for a ruling because its bytes differ. A lockstep test that passes stops nothing. The one moment it could act as a byte standard is when a harmless difference fails it, and the decision then requires the test to be changed, not the bytes matched. Amended FR-002 also owes no ask or ruling for that. So the test never operates as the struck standard. Rewriting tests that pass now would add nothing toward 'everything works'. Condition: the amended engine-plan.md and FR-002 must say this plainly. Changing the failing test is the expected response, never a reason to chase the old bytes.

decisions.why: Judged on the rulings' text, now carried. The ground is not that refitting broke deliberate composition (awkward, not impossible, and existing behavior the GM did not ask to keep). It is that the standard these sheets miss is not a 'known bug' or a research finding in the GM's words. -room-layout records the bands as 'the project's guess around a few measured houses (labeled as such, with no claim behind them)', and -room-scope repeats that. The GM's measure for a map is 'so long as the changes don't violate our research findings' and FR-002 'must pass its checks and hold its research claims'. Every one of these sheets passes every check, and none is held to a claim the bands carry. -room-sizes' 'correcting a sheet to match the research needs no permission' rested on three measured houses. A room two to eight times the largest of three measured rooms lies outside a small sample. It does not contradict a recorded research finding, and -room-scope expressly narrows -room-sizes on that ground. The ruling holds for each sheet separately: Ochiba and Ubame (deliberate items named), Hayakawa (none named, but it misses the same guess band and nothing else), and the county example. The county example is regenerated from its program, and the block says the bands apply to generated plans, but no review found its rooms defective. The findings that started the work concern the round-trip sheet (-room-scope), so no known defect of the county example is carried. Purpose test: the GM's rule exists so step 3b is not ported on top of known breakage. The round-trip sheet, the placer's own test and the one sheet these findings were made on, is fixed (D3a), so the purpose is met. The arbiter's ruling carried this route. The GM's words, not the ruling, are what make it legitimate.

decisions.summary: make static, make rust-test, make quick after the last edit; then plan review, claims round, gated make land
decisions.why: The project's standing exits; nothing added or skipped.

decisions.summary: Fix the disc-ink and several-parts-ink leader defects in the Rust placer/hand sheet AND the kept Python placer.py/hand_sheet.py.

The kept Python still draws the pool sheets (FR-003), so fixing Rust alone would leave the bug live; the 2026-11-10 'no longer changing it' words concern deleting tests, and the later fix-as-we-go words govern a known defect.

decisions.summary: InkPart/Subject.ink/drawn_ink/nearest_ink: a disc's ink is its drawn curve, a several-part subject carries every part's ink, leader_of scores to that ink and leader_to_ink measures a disc by its curve, so the drawn leader is the scored one.
