decisions.summary: DISC_SAG_PX = 0.05 px sag bound, at least 8 samples, claimed as a CONVENTION.
decisions.why: An implementation constant for the fix, claimed; settles nothing the request or spec left open in a narrower direction.

decisions.summary: A stroke is chosen by its line's distance, end drawn back by the half-width; on a tie an outline before a stroke and the wider stroke before the narrower; two alternative forms priced and rejected.
decisions.why: A design choice within the fix, claimed as a CONVENTION in both copies; pinned on both orders by tests. Not a narrowing of anything asked.

decisions.summary: New/changed CONVENTION claims (which subjects carry ink, which part a leader ends on, where a leader ends); Rust's standing finds a seat's subject by kind, outline and angle rather than by sampled-float ink.
decisions.why: Claims follow the changed behavior. The standing change loosens a float match between copies, which is in the direction of the GM's 2026-11-18 rule against exactness standards.

decisions.summary: Four new Rust tests, red before the fix, in leader_tests.rs split from tests.rs past the 1,000-line bar.
decisions.why: Enforcement of the fix the GM asked for (fix known bugs); the split is constitution X housekeeping.

decisions.summary: Hand sheet held.json re-taken from the fixed Python with a twelfth sheet; one earlier answer (the prefixed sheet's well) moved and is named; placer held.json re-answered, none moved.
decisions.why: FR-002's clause for a check or behavior fixed on purpose: its expected result changes as fixed, named. The GM 2026-11-18: 'it needs to be okay to have checks pass as we make those fixes'.

decisions.summary: On the pool, one seat (Ubame's fire-water tubs) and five leaders move; four pages differ from HEAD's render; pack-audit and size-table exit 0 on all six sheets.
decisions.why: FR-002 and the GM 2026-11-17/18: maps may change so long as everything works; the sheets pass their checks. Not an exception to be ruled.

decisions.summary: The exits (approach items 6 and 9) rest on red/green runs, probes and the audits passing; 'byte for byte', 'manifest unchanged', 'report is HEAD's' and 'placed text is the same' are labeled observations, not bars.
decisions.why: No requirement in the block holds a port or change to bitwise agreement, which the GM struck on 2026-11-18.

decisions.summary: A known defect (a leader past a stroke's end ends on a round cap the sheet may not draw, up to half-width short of a flat end's ink) is left out of T192 and drafted as its own task, before step 3b.
decisions.why: T192's own scope leaves a known defect, so it is classed narrowing, but the GM's words set the unit as the step: 'fix all known bugs in each step before moving on to porting the next step'. The block's drafted task line says 'fixed with a test red first, before step 3b', in both copies, and the dispatch states it is filed as T193 ordered before step 3b (not verified here: the bundle forbids reading the repository). The purpose - no known defect carried into the next step - is untouched. No pool leader currently ends so (caps.py).

decisions.summary: Research page 0242's leader bullet gains the sentence that a leader ending at the drawn feature's nearest point is a map drawing convention no source fixes; the claims cite it.
decisions.why: Records the convention the fix rests on so its claims cite a page; historical accuracy is the research ladder's, not this review's. The page stays under its cap.

decisions.summary: The reader keeps stroke-linecap (inherited, square/round, else SVG's butt); stroke_band draws a stroke as SVG does at its ends; leader_to_ink and nearest_ink measure by that band, in the Rust and the kept Python alike.
decisions.why: A known step-3a defect (leaders stopping short of or past a butt end, a block within the half-width drawing no leader) fixed in every living copy before step 3b, exactly what the GM asked on 2026-11-18 ('fix all known bugs in each step before moving on'). The pool reach (no caption moved) and the moved held answer are outputs changing as fixed, which FR-002 permits.

decisions.summary: nearest_ink chooses the part whose drawn edge is nearest (a stroke by its band, a closed outline drawn out by its own stroke half-width) and ends on its nearest drawn point; leader_to_ink draws an outline out by its stroke; of three measured forms the third is kept.
decisions.why: Brings the code to research page 0242's rule, 'it ends at the nearest drawn point', answering impl-drift's 4 DRIFTED; the rejected forms were rejected because they put leaders on the wrong ink (the dashed passage line), not to narrow anything. 28 hand-sheet and 10 compound leader ends move, no caption: changes as fixed under FR-002 and constitution XIV.

decisions.summary: A block of a stepped building, or a scatter's member, carries the ink of every closed part drawn with its box (drawn_as/_drawn_as), so a block drawn as a fill plus a stroked outline ends on the outline's stroke.
decisions.why: Part of ending at the nearest drawn point: Hayakawa's RESIDENCE leader ended inside the outline's stroke. A defect of this step, fixed in both copies.

decisions.summary: An exact tie keeps T192's order (an outline before a stroke, then the wider), recorded as a CONVENTION claim 'a tie between parts'; measured that the first two orders decide no pool leader.
decisions.why: Keeps an existing convention for a case the research rule leaves open; narrows nothing the GM asked for. FR-002 lists 'the order of ties' among outputs that may differ, so no exactness standard is applied.

decisions.summary: The claims cite 0242's drawing page in both copies; 'a stroke's drawn band' is a new CONVENTION claim; the research page itself is not edited because it already says what the code does.
decisions.why: Bookkeeping that ties the fix to its research ground; no scope change. The 0242 tie-order sentence the dispatch places in T194 is not a decision of this block.

decisions.summary: held.json re-taken from the fixed Python with a thirteenth sheet (LED_CAPS); one of 29 earlier answers (the tax barge) moves seat; the placer's held.json re-answered unchanged.
decisions.why: Tests that enforce the requested fix (red on HEAD, green on the clone) serve the request; an expected result that changes because a bug is fixed is changed as fixed (FR-002's exception, SC-004).

decisions.summary: The held walls' captions take rank 18 over rank 2 because rank 2's leader, run from the block's corner to a flat end parallel to it, grazes the pen's gap; the block rules a corner-to-parallel-edge leader 'no defect', and no pool leader ended past a stroke's end on HEAD.
decisions.why: Checked against the block's own rule and 0242: such a leader still ends on the drawn ink at the nearest drawn point, the same geometry any building edge gives, so it is not a known bug being carried past the step. It is behavior of the scorer on a test sheet, and the GM's fix-as-we-go clause is not narrowed by it.

decisions.summary: All six pool sheets regenerated by make map, manifests unchanged; pack-audit and size-table exit 0 on every sheet and both copies' placed text; size tables differ only in moved leaders' rows.
decisions.why: The checks must pass and the research claims hold; they do. 'Every pack-audit report HEAD's' is a measured reach, not a standard the work is held to: the block itself accepts moved leaders and a moved held answer, so no exactness standard is applied.

decisions.summary: The reader keeps a path's curves only by their end points (Hoshigaoka's arc-drawn rope ring read as a 10 px line doubled back); left to a drafted task, fixed red-first in both copies before step 3b.
decisions.why: The GM's boundary is 'before moving on to porting the next step', not 'in this task': the drafted line says before step 3b and both copies. The dispatch says it is filed as T194, ordered before step 3b; that ordering was supplied by the dispatch and not verified, as the bundle forbids reading the repository. Had it been carried into step 3b it would be NOT LEGITIMATE.

decisions.summary: No stroke's stroke-dasharray is read, so a leader to a dashed stroke may end in a gap; left to the same drafted task, before step 3b, both copies.
decisions.why: Same boundary and same filing as the curves gap (T194 before step 3b, per the dispatch, not verified here). Not carried into the next step.

decisions.summary: stroke-linejoin is unread, so a bend's or stroked corner's outside is drawn round where SVG's miter reaches further (1.86 px at a 9 px right angle); measured that no pool leader so ends; left to a drafted task before step 3b, both copies.
decisions.why: Same boundary: filed as T194, ordered before step 3b, per the dispatch (not verified here); the drafted line names both copies and a red-first test. Not carried into the next step.

decisions.summary: path_points (both copies) returns each subpath and its Z; Beziers flattened by Wang's bound, smooth forms reflected, arcs per SVG 1.1 F.6; sag DISC_SAG_PX (convention 0.05 px) divided by the element's largest stretch
decisions.why: Fixes a known step-3a reader defect (a leader not ending on the ink as SVG draws it) in this step, as the GM asked 2026-11-18 ('fix all known bugs in each step before moving on'); the sag reuses an existing convention, no constant moves.

decisions.summary: each subpath its own shape, Z closes its stroke with a join and no cap, path/polyline fill read as inherited; an unknown cap/join/limit ignored so the inherited one stands, replacing T193's unknown-cap-as-butt
decisions.why: Each is a measured reader defect (phantom joining segment, missing closing side, fill read without inheritance, T193's unknown cap) fixed in the step it was found, per the GM's fix-as-we-go rule; the changed maps fall under FR-002 (outputs may differ so long as everything works).

decisions.summary: dashes drawn (each dash its own stroke with caps, from stroke-dashoffset, scaled), chosen after measuring that a drawn pool leader ends on a dashed stroke and that drawing them moves no pool caption
decisions.why: Implements 0242/0330's rule that a leader ends on the nearest drawn point; a gap is not ink. Widens correctness, narrows nothing the GM asked for.

decisions.summary: stroke-linejoin/miterlimit read and inherited, joins drawn per SVG 1.1 (miter, bevel past the limit, round disc); closed outlines measured round then each miter tried; CORNER_EPS a 1e-9 px rounding guard keeping the round point when a miter point is nearer only by rounding
decisions.why: A drawn-ink fix in this step; CORNER_EPS is a rounding tie-guard that decides nothing about place, introduced to stop a leader crossing a roof edge on a rounding artifact, not a carve-out from any requested behavior.

decisions.summary: a zero-length stroke draws nothing for butt, a disc for round, a square for square (SVG 2 13.5.5); nearest_ink answers None where nothing is drawn; ink_nearest deleted and leader_to_ink measures with nearest_ink so the scored and drawn leader agree
decisions.why: Resolves T193's impl-drift findings (DRIFTED, MISLABELED) in this step, as fix-as-we-go asks; one measure for scored and drawn removes a divergence rather than narrowing anything.

decisions.summary: the leader claims re-cite 0330; 0242's leader bullet moved word for word to new page 0330 with its note, 0330 adding the tie order, corners and dashes; QGIS archive record names 0330's notes
decisions.why: Keeps the research claims the fixed code carries on a page, as FR-002 requires the claims to hold; the split follows the record's size rule and moves text verbatim. No request clause is narrowed.

decisions.summary: new stroke_tests.rs from markup through HEAD's APIs, red on HEAD with T193's cap test, green on the clone
decisions.why: Enforcement of the requested fixes (a test that fails only when the fix is absent); serves the fix-as-we-go request.

decisions.summary: the kept Python placer/hand_sheet fixed alike; held.json re-taken with two more sheets, its 30 earlier answers unchanged; placer's held.json re-answered, none of 60 moved
decisions.why: The GM asked known bugs be fixed in every live copy; the kept Python still runs (FR-003) and is fixed in lockstep. The Rust/Python agreement is reported as an observation, not held as an exactness standard.

decisions.summary: of 190 pool captions, 5 seats and 8 leaders move, each laid to its change; Hayakawa's caption cost 20,500 for 19,500; leader ends move 0.0015 to 0.31 px; compound sheets' well captions move
decisions.why: FR-002 (T180) and the GM 2026-11-18: maps may change so long as everything works; every audit exits 0 and each move is traced to a fix. A fix changing a map is expected, never a regression.

decisions.summary: the kept Python seats the four sheets in 25.9 s against 20.4 s on HEAD, one run each, recorded only
decisions.why: No requirement binds the kept Python's speed (it is being deleted under FR-001); recording it rather than acting narrows no request clause.

decisions.summary: a filled path's hole read as filled, a dashed closed outline measured solid, an unfilled closed part's inside counted as ink, the audit's path walk keeping an arc by its end point, and 0242's next split: left to T195, filed and ordered before step 3b
decisions.why: The GM's rule is per step: 'fix all known bugs in each step before moving on to porting the next step'. T195 is filed and ordered before step 3b's first port, so every known step-3a defect (and the step-2 audit crop found now) is fixed before the next step; splitting the work across tasks within the step narrows nothing the GM asked.

decisions.summary: make decide/task-add spin from fancy_regex's step limit fixed in the plan and task crates with this task, tests red on the old code; the rest of the class left to T185, also before step 3b
decisions.why: A known tooling bug fixed as found, its remainder filed before the next step, consistent with the GM's fix-as-we-go rule and the 2026-11-16/18 efficiency instructions.

decisions.summary: Every Regex::new / RegexBuilder::new under rust/ goes through l7r_guard::shared::regex::build/builder, compiled with no backtrack step limit; the three site-set limits (apply-edits' EDIT, checks::pages) and T151's `unbounded` fold into it.
decisions.why: Fixes the known bug T151/T194 found (a search past fancy_regex's 1,000,000-step default reads as no match, replace_all panics, a flattened iterator never ends) at every site, which is what the GM's 2026-11-18 'fix all known bugs in each step before moving on' asks. Dropping the three site-set limits for the shared, larger (none) limit narrows nothing: no site loses an answer it gave.

decisions.summary: Every find_iter / captures_iter / regex split ends on its first error with .map_while(Result::ok) (spelled std::result::Result::ok where a crate shadows Result), replacing .flatten() / .filter_map(Result::ok) and three .count()s.
decisions.why: Removes the infinite repeat of the same Err that made scans spin, the same known bug; uses the adapter T194 already used.

decisions.summary: LABEL, whose greedy lookaheads overflow fancy_regex's fixed VM stack on a megabyte sentence and answered 'no label' in error, is replaced by has_label: three plain linear searches (the measured word, an ISO date, an opening parenthesis; or an m: key), pinned by a 1.2 MB labeled/unlabeled test; plan crate 128 tests pass.
decisions.why: Last round's BLOCKED narrowing (a known bug left standing) is now fixed rather than carved out. Editing the plan crate, though the task line scopes its census to the crates outside plan and task, is fixing a known bug where it was found, as the GM asked. Under FR-002 (T180) the replacement is held to doing its job - its existing tests and the new megabyte case pass - not to a match-for-match equivalence with LABEL, so none is owed.

decisions.summary: The eight patterns found quadratic by the leading-word probe (PLAN_RECORDED, SIDE, LOOP, GIT_WRITE, MAKE_WRITE, PGREP_F, APPLY, SEARCHER_COUNT) are anchored at their segment's first trigger with an atomic group; 7-12 ms on 100 KB; answers agreed on random texts.
decisions.why: Lifting the step limit would otherwise turn these known silent failures into multi-second-to-unbounded runs; fixing them is the known-bug fix the GM asked for, and the random-text agreement is the plan's own evidence that they still do their job, not an exactness standard imposed on the port.

decisions.summary: Patterns built at run time (format!, read from files: coord's KEY, prereq's, diffrun's cases, the blocked list) are not timed, now run with no step limit, and their scans end quietly on an error as the backstop; the leading-word probe reached 533 of 982 literal patterns.
decisions.why: The GM's words are 'fix all known bugs'. Unlike LABEL last round, no measured failure stands among these sites: the bundle reports no erring or slow run-time pattern, and the plan states plainly what was not shown linear. The changed failure mode for such a pattern, should one exist (a long run, caught by the tests' 20 s bound and the stuck-command tooling, in place of a quiet wrong answer), is no narrowing of anything requested; no FR in the spec bounds a regex's run time.

decisions.summary: A real-tree test in the checks crate (documents/regex_scans.rs) fails on a Regex::new/RegexBuilder::new outside the shared constructor, a find_iter/captures_iter followed by anything but .map_while(Result::ok) or .next(), and a regex split followed by .flatten()/.filter_map(Result::ok); self-test seeds each form.
decisions.why: A test whose only effect is to keep the requested fix fixed (GM 2026-09-20): it fails, it does not refuse or rewrite work, and with the fix removed it has nothing to check.

decisions.summary: The new regression tests are each bounded by a 20 s timeout (T194's convention) so a spin fails rather than hangs; twelve shown red on HEAD's code and green on the clone.
decisions.why: Pins the fix; the bound is a failure ceiling, not the tests' run time, so FR-008's tenth-of-a-second bar is not relaxed by it.

decisions.summary: Exits: make format, make rust-test, make static, make hooks-test HOOKS_ALL=1, make quick, plan review, gated make land; an lld incremental-object fault cleared with cargo clean -p, no source change.
decisions.why: The standing gate; nothing skipped.

decisions.summary: Ordered after T194 and before step 3b's first port; 'Performance work? No - a defect fixed'; differentials and pool manifests n/a (tooling).
decisions.why: The order is exactly the GM's 'fix all known bugs in each step before moving on to porting the next step'. The task changes tooling regex scans, no drawn output, so no differential or pool manifest is touched; and it fixes wrong answers and hangs, a defect, rather than claiming a speed saving under the 2026-11-12 pre-approval's conditions.

decisions.summary: A FREE_TEXT list; each named value becomes a simple variable holding its text as given (override NAME := $(value NAME)), exported, read in recipes as "$$NAME".
decisions.why: This is the fix of the known bug T182's claims round found (a backtick in a claim key run as a command), and of the same bug's second form it measured (make expanding a $ in NOTE). The GM 2026-11-18: 'in general we should fix all known bugs in each step before moving on'.

decisions.summary: l7r-gate's flags unchanged (--units "$$UNITS"); sub-makes stop re-passing free text on their command lines; SET_DOWN_OK/HOLD_OK prefixes dropped as the exported variable is the one read.
decisions.why: Keeps every caller of the gate's flags as it is; the sub-make change is the same fix applied to the places that re-quoted the value. Nothing narrowed.

decisions.summary: The 59 free-text names on FREE_TEXT and every quoted use, required-argument check and longer word holding one rewritten across the listed recipes.
decisions.why: Applies the fix to every site of the same known bug rather than the one target that surfaced it, which is what 'fix all known bugs' asks. It removes no behavior a caller relies on: the values now arrive as typed.

decisions.summary: Paths (FILE, FILES, OUT, ... TRANSCRIPT, IN) left as $(NAME).
decisions.why: The GM's words are 'fix all known bugs'. A known bug here is a value a target is meant to take that today's form runs or mangles; the plan converted URLs and patterns on exactly that format ground (RFC 3986 allows $, patterns carry * and ?). A path in this tree holds no shell syntax (the block's survey, part A item 4) and the bundle shows no path value mangled, so leaving paths is not leaving a known bug. Non-blocking note: FILES and PAGES are list-shaped; if a caller passes one holding a $ or backtick, it moves to FREE_TEXT like the other lists.

decisions.summary: Numbers (F, ROW, ... BOX), enums (MODE, MODEL, ... AS) and flags (FULL, BATCH, CONSULTED, HOOKS_ALL, ENGINE) left as $(NAME).
decisions.why: A number, an enum from a closed set or a boolean flag cannot carry a valid value holding shell syntax, so no known bug is left; the request ('fix all known bugs') is met.

decisions.summary: Ids (T, TASK, ... NAME, RELEASE, INTO, TAGS, AFFECTS, KEEP, DROP, ONLY, COMMIT, BASE, AGAINST, REVS, SINCE, UNTIL, DATE) left as $(NAME).
decisions.why: Task ids, slugs, git revisions and dates have formats that hold no $, backtick or $( (git rev syntax such as HEAD^ or @{1} is unharmed by make or by a quoted shell word), and the bundle shows no id value mangled; so no known bug is left and 'fix all known bugs' is met. Non-blocking note: the list-shaped ids (AGENTS, TRIGGERS, TAGS, REVS, AFFECTS, KEEP, DROP, ONLY) and NAME are the ones to move to FREE_TEXT if any is ever found carrying free text.

decisions.summary: URLS, MATCH, NONE, SHARD, EXTRA, IMAGES, DIRS, LAND and SUITES on FREE_TEXT, split by the shell (unquoted $$NAME, or a set -- loop adding a flag per word) instead of make's $(foreach).
decisions.why: Closes the two known bugs the block names in these lists (make expanding a $ in a URL, a backtick running inside the quotes) while keeping one argument a word as before. This is the item the previous round blocked, now fixed as asked.

decisions.summary: set -f before splitting the word lists; a pattern in EXTRA or IMAGES is no longer expanded by the recipe's shell, a directory naming the same files.
decisions.why: For URLs and MATCH/NONE/SHARD patterns it is part of the fix (a ? in a URL globbed to a fixture file, the test's case). For EXTRA/IMAGES it is a behavior difference the fix does not strictly need, but under the no-exactness rule it is a finding only if something stops working, and the bundle shows no caller passing check-bundle a pattern, with a directory giving the same files. A caller in the tree that hands EXTRA or IMAGES a glob would change this ruling.

decisions.summary: tests/hooks/test-make-only-hooks.sh section 6: the real Makefile against a stub gate, hostile values through a flag, TICK_NOTE, a required-argument check, a sub-make, URLS and MATCH; plus a scan failing any recipe line handing a FREE_TEXT name to the shell as $(NAME); red on HEAD's Makefile, green on this one.
decisions.why: Enforcement of the requested fix: delete the fix and the test has nothing left to check. Verification, not new behavior (GM 2026-09-20).

decisions.summary: The suites' deps index holds the root Makefile as a shared helper, and the hooks stamp area holds Makefile, each with a test.
decisions.why: Without it a Makefile-only edit leaves the make-only suite skipped, so the requested fix's test would not run on the change it guards; it only makes the enforcement of what was asked actually run. Not unrequested scope.

decisions.summary: The filed command re-run on the real gate (the country-shrine key with backticks), then hooks-test HOOKS_ALL=1, static and quick green.
decisions.why: Shows the filed bug fixed and everything working; no decision beyond the spec.

decisions.summary: Constitution XIV defines a defect as a wrong outcome (map reads wrong, research finding contradicted, check passes bad/refuses good work, tool crashes/hangs/refuses valid input/answers wrongly) and what is not one; XIII's 'each step's known defects' points at it; a claim the code does not literally match where behavior is fine is fixed by restating the claim (the tolerance rule).
decisions.why: The GM approved 'that tolerance rule' and asked what guideline changes would make 'don't spend a lot of time fixing things which are not actually wrong' obvious (request.md 2026-11-19); the definition restates his own words (works, in line with research, maps look fine) and gives his 2026-11-18 'fix all known bugs' its object.

decisions.summary: Constitution to 2.36.0 (MINOR) and its stale 2.35.0 footer corrected with it.
decisions.why: The amendment is the guideline change asked for; the version bump and footer correction are the constitution's own amendment bookkeeping.

decisions.summary: One line each in root and research/ CLAUDE.md; the four review agents carry the definition beside FIX AS WE GO; plan template gains a XIV entry; checklist item 12 'Before any fix' and a 'Found and left?' line in make task-add's section; docs/gm-rulings.md records the GM's words.
decisions.why: Each is a place a session or reviewer reads before acting; the GM asked for project-guideline changes so the thing is 'noticed and caught before I come back'. Placing the definition in agents that launch without CLAUDE.md is what makes reviewers catch it.

decisions.summary: impl-drift names each DRIFTED verdict's fix (fix: claim / fix: code) and effect inside the note, verdict line form unchanged; make claims-checked refuses a DRIFTED line with no fix, in triage::vet.
decisions.why: Enforcement of the request: its only effect is to force each drift to be classed claim-vs-code at the point it is judged, which is the 'noticed and caught' the GM asked for; it refuses nothing beyond a DRIFTED line lacking the fix the request makes necessary.

decisions.summary: The refusal checks fix: claim|code only; effect: is asked by the agent file and shown in the refusal's form but not refused when missing.
decisions.why: The GM asked for nothing about an effect field; a refusal narrower than the agent's ask narrows the session's own mechanism, not the request, and avoids refusing good replies on free text.

decisions.summary: claims-accept writes its DRIFTED lines through reply::record, not vet, so an arbiter-accepted drift whose note predates the rule is not refused.
decisions.why: This carves a case out of the new refusal. Purpose test: the request is that sessions stop spending time 'fixing' things that are not wrong. An already-accepted known drift's pre-rule note is not wrong; refusing it would force sessions to rewrite correct, already-adjudicated records, the exact waste the GM asked to end, and by the definition he approved a check that refuses good work is a defect. Literal application defeats the request's stated purpose. One case, one class (arbiter-accepted lines); new filed departures still carry fix: code per the next decision, so the refusal's purpose is not gutted.

decisions.summary: A filed departure's note becomes 'known (NNN Tnn): <departure>; fix: code; effect: <effect>'; nothing parses the 'known (' prefix (observed 2026-11-19, grep).
decisions.why: Brings filed departures under the same fix/effect naming; changes no parsed form.

decisions.summary: Checklist item 12 is marked '(asked where written)': a section with no 12. line passes the approach gate, one that writes it must answer it (empty or <...> placeholder refused); items 1-11 owed as before; make task-add still writes 12 and spec-fidelity reads it. Required, it would refuse the tick of 58 open tasks whose sections predate it (observed 2026-11-19, shell loop).
decisions.why: Narrows the reach of the plan's own enforcement device, not anything the GM worded. Purpose test: requiring 12 retroactively would refuse ticks of 58 pre-existing, already-reviewed sections whose work is not wrong and force edits (and per-block plan re-reviews) to fix sections that are not wrong - defeating the request's purpose concretely, and a check refusing good work is a defect under the definition the GM approved. Every new section written by make task-add carries 12, the agents and constitution carry the definition, and the fix/effect refusal stands, so the request's catch-it-before-the-GM purpose is not gutted. The required read for a search or scan growing faster than its input targets exactly the operation-count failure. Any other wrong outcome stays under FR-002 and the fix-as-we-go rule. BOUND: the ruling covers only code with no search, placement, layout, optimization or iterative fitting. Code that does any of these is an algorithm under this rule, whatever it is labeled, and is not covered. Ported code later found to grow faster than its input falls back under the rebuild rule. decisions.summary: T214 is closed as already done by T213: T213 deleted pytest, and with it the make-only guard's pytest branch that refused a quoted mention, so there is nothing more to change and the tick records it.
decisions.why: The defect T156's scoping found is a check refusing good work (constitution XIV; FR-002's exception for a guard that refuses correct work). The GM asked 2026-11-18 that known bugs be fixed in each step. Removing the branch together with pytest is inside FR-001b, which deletes the Python tests and pytest. Nothing that was asked is left undone or excluded.

decisions.summary: Done is measured by the existing test make_only_hooks/tests.rs::a_pytest_command_or_mention_is_left_alone passing on main, which pins that a pytest command or mention goes through.
decisions.why: The test only fails if the fix is undone, so it enforces the fix and adds no scope. The make-only guard keeps covering what FR-005 asks it to cover. Only the branch for a tool that FR-001b deleted is gone.

decisions.summary: Ordered after T213; budget is the tick alone; exits are green (test in place) or red (recorded, set down, impossibility claim to make arbiter-ask).
decisions.why: Sequencing and procedure only; it neither narrows nor widens the request.

decisions.summary: Remove or re-point the tooling that names deleted scripts or missing targets: make scatter-bases and the two agent files naming its deleted script, cache-audit in .PHONY with no rule, make done FULL=1's perf-gate with no rule (passed by running nothing), measure_hooks' tips naming the deleted make cov-file, sync-with-main.sh's unused variable and its seeding of a dead roll store into every new clone.
decisions.why: Each is a tool that runs nothing, runs a deleted script or answers wrongly - a defect under constitution XIV as the GM's 2026-11-19 wording bounds it (a check passing by running nothing, a tool answering wrongly) - left behind by FR-001's port and deletions; the GM's 2026-11-18 'we should fix all known bugs in each step before moving on to porting the next step' asks for exactly this. The unused variable is a one-line cleanup in the same script, adds no behavior and narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: make map with no GEN, which defaulted to a file that no longer exists, is refused with a message naming its forms rather than given a new default.
decisions.why: A default that points at a missing file is a tool failing on its own default; refusing with the valid forms fixes the wrong outcome without inventing a default the GM never chose. Nothing a caller relied on is removed: the old default could not run.

decisions.summary: A new section of the make-only suite (no recipe runs a missing script, every phase make done runs has a rule, make map without GEN refused naming its forms), plus tree and cohort tests, written red first.
decisions.why: Tests whose only effect is to make the fixes above happen and stay fixed; delete the fixes and the checks have nothing left to check. Enforcement of what was asked, not scope (GM 2026-09-20).

decisions.summary: The open land-route question, measured (observed 2026-11-19, l7r-gate delta engine-paths on the Ubame sheet's path): an edit to a tracked hand-sheet/pool svg was not counted as engine, so it landed DIRECT with no make done and no pool sweep; a tracked pool svg now counts as engine in the tree crate (delta.rs) and the landing's cohort list (cohort.rs), red first.
decisions.why: A measured defect - a sheet edit skipping the checks and T211's pool sweep that exist to judge it, i.e. the gate passing work it never checked. It widens the gate to the exact class of file the sweep exists for and no further (pool svgs only; the notes-only edit is not swept in here), so it narrows nothing and adds no behavior beyond making an existing check reach the file it was meant to check.

decisions.summary: More .PHONY names with no rule that pass by running nothing (perf-review on every push among them), a dead cache-audit guard, and a notes-only edit skipping the sweep: found during the task and filed as their own task (2026-11-19) rather than fixed in T218.
decisions.why: Not a decision to leave defects unfixed: they are recorded and scheduled as a task, which is how work is split, and this task is T157's tooling cleanup, not a port step. The GM's rule is that known defects are fixed 'in each step before moving on to porting the next step'; that rule binds at the next port step's start, so the filed task must land before any next engine/port step begins - a plan that let it slip past that boundary would be the finding, and this section does not do so.

decisions.summary: First of T157's landings, before T219; one gated landing; exits green on the suites red-then-green, make quick, make static, make hooks-test; red recorded and set down, a cannot-be-done claim ruled through make arbiter-ask.
decisions.why: Sequencing and process the spec leaves open; nothing asked is narrowed and no exception is taken.

decisions.summary: Remove eleven .PHONY names with no rule whose job left with the Python engine, with every caller (the push's perf-review call and its seam), and the docs and agent files that name them; perf-audit.md marked dormant and pointed at make work-budget and make budget-sheets.
decisions.why: Each target passed while checking nothing (observed 2026-11-19, .PHONY against rules, make -n), which is a defect under XIV: a check passing the bad. Removing a call that ran nothing changes no behavior except the false pass. The tooling port (2026-11-07 request) and the 2026-11-18 'fix all known bugs in each step' cover it. The performance review the GM wants is not dropped: it is pointed at the work-budget review, and T224 makes that review real before T220.

decisions.summary: cohort-landing is kept, now refusing with its reason instead of passing; the cohort gate states this at the current port switch.
decisions.why: Feature 444 FR-023 has make land roll no landing cohort while the port switch stands at rust-only, and brings the cohort back when the switch is thrown to integrated. The caller states that make land calls cohort-landing only when the switch is not rust-only, so the refusal blocks no landing now. If the switch is thrown before feature 444 restores the job, an honest refusal is what FR-023's return requires, not a silent pass.

decisions.summary: A test refuses any .PHONY name with no rule, red first on HEAD's Makefile.
decisions.why: Enforcement of D1's fix. It fails only when a target that runs nothing comes back, so it serves the request rather than adding scope.

decisions.summary: Remove gate_write_hooks' dead cache-audit guard.
decisions.why: Dead code tied to a removed target. Removing it is part of the same cleanup and changes no live behavior.

decisions.summary: A pool sheet's .notes.md, which the sweep reads, counts as engine for the land route, red first; the frozen tree's notes stay excluded.
decisions.why: Before this change, a notes-only edit skipped the checks that read it, which is a defect (a wrong outcome). The caller states that the frozen tree's notes are read by no check (the sweep reads pool/ only), so excluding them leaves no input unchecked and narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: make hooks-test runs the cohort gate's own suite, which no gate ran.
decisions.why: A suite that no gate runs is a check that never runs. Wiring it in is a fix and adds no behavior.

decisions.summary: Found and left: the work-budget review prints suspended and exits 0, and the green-gate stamp misses pool-only changes. Both are filed as T224, which lands before T220 (the next port step), with the reason recorded and also stated on T224's own line.
decisions.why: Both are defects (a check passing having judged nothing; a stamp missing changes). The GM, 2026-11-18: 'we should fix all known bugs in each step before moving on to porting the next step'. Filing them as a separate task that lands before T220 honors that rule. The step boundary is kept, so nothing that was asked is narrowed. This satisfies route (a) of the previous BLOCKED.

decisions.summary: Stale command names in guards, gate messages and docs are filed as T225 (wording only).
decisions.why: The 2026-11-19 rule (constitution XIV v2.36.0) says a defect is a wrong outcome, and wording that misleads no check or map is not one. Leaving it for a later task is within what was asked and needs no ruling. If a stale name ever made a guard refuse or pass wrongly, it would be a defect, and the block states that none does.

decisions.summary: Rebuild the pipeline's walk and generation key from a derivation written blind to l7r/diagram/pipeline/, in feature 443/444's pool-sheet form with the two trees as its sheets (the stage has no households).
decisions.why: The GM's 2026-11-19 words (rebuild from derivations, not port the Python's mistakes) and the 2026-10-30 rule carried by T199 (not re-implementing the old, inefficient algorithms) ask for exactly this; using the two trees as sheets adapts the form to a stage without households and excludes nothing.

decisions.summary: Per-entry read records replaced by one shared table of distinct reads (path, stat, digest, maps that read it), with the ordering that removes an affected map's entry before its row takes a new digest, and a table lock.
decisions.why: A design detail inside the derivation, adopted on the work-budget agent's first-round LOOSE finding; it serves the goal of work in proportion to what changed and keeps no map served stale. Nothing asked for is dropped.

decisions.summary: Set the pipeline's work budget from the SOUND derivation (2,064 counted operations for a warm unchanged run) with make budget-set PHASE=pipeline.
decisions.why: The budget is the enforcement of the GM's efficiency rule for the rewrite; it serves the request and restricts nothing it asked for.

decisions.summary: T219 lands only the derivation and the budget; the rebuild is T220-T222 as phase tasks with the guard on, after T218 and T223.
decisions.why: Sequencing: derivation before rebuild is the order the GM's 2026-11-19 plan approval names; no part of the work is dropped, only placed in following tasks of the same step.

decisions.summary: Two found defects (the Mode A page writer reporting only files it found, leaving a later-created looked-for file's sheet cached stale; a read first recorded on a miss hashed after the engine read it) left to T221, written onto its line.
decisions.why: Both are defects (a stale sheet served is a wrong outcome), and the GM's 2026-11-18 rule is that each step's known defects are fixed before the next step's port begins. T221 is part of this same rebuild (T220-T222), so the defects are fixed within the step, not carried into the next one; T219 itself changes no code that could fix them.

decisions.summary: make work-budget-review stops being a printf that printed suspended and exited 0; it becomes l7r-gate measure work-budget-review, holding each accepted hamlet stage at its sizes against its accepted figure and twice its budget (the two holds the deleted Python made)
decisions.why: Restores the job the deleted Python review did (FR-002: a replaced piece does its job for its callers; a ported check still does its job). A review that passes every push is a check passing bad work, a defect under the GM's 2026-11-18 'fix broken things as we find them'; it also serves the 2026-11-19 plan that step 3a be measured against a derived work budget.

decisions.summary: each Mode A pool-sheet stage held to twice its budget per sheet
decisions.why: Applies the existing feature 443/444 budget rule (FR-022's leeway) to stages the Rust driver now counts; enforcement of the work budget the GM's 2026-11-19 plan and 2026-10-30 efficiency rule rest on. It narrows nothing; whether 2x is the right leeway is a design matter, not fidelity.

decisions.summary: the pipeline stage, which nothing counts yet, is printed UNCOUNTED with its reason rather than held, until T220-T222 supply its counters
decisions.why: Holding a stage against its budget is physically impossible without a count; the counters are owed by named tasks T220-T222, the next in order, and the stage is printed with its reason, never passed silently, so the review's purpose (no stage lands over budget unnoticed) is not gutted.

decisions.summary: the waterward stage, 'whose reference roll has a pond', is printed with that reason rather than held
decisions.why: Same physical impossibility as 3a: the block states nothing counts this stage on its reference roll, and the review cannot hold what has no count; it is printed with its reason, never passed silently. Unlike 3a the block names no owner for this reason; the bundle does not say whether the missing count is a counter defect. If it is, the GM's 2026-11-18 rule ('fix all known bugs in each step before moving on to porting the next step') requires it settled (T226 or its own task) before the next step's port begins.

decisions.summary: an accepted stage missing from a run is refused with the fix named
decisions.why: Keeps the review from passing a stage by its absence; enforcement of the review's own job.

decisions.id: T224-5 counts kept by the files they read
decisions.summary: counts cached keyed on the files they read, so an unmoved push costs about 0.3 s
decisions.why: Efficiency of the tooling the GM repeatedly asked for (2026-11-11, 2026-11-19); the count reruns whenever any file it reads moves, so no case is skipped.

decisions.summary: make land's fallback that ran the count without writing it is removed
decisions.why: Removes a path that ran the count with no effect; the block's goal is that no push lands a stage over budget, and removing an unchecked route widens rather than narrows the hold.

decisions.summary: the green-gate stamp's diagram area covers pool .json, .svg and .notes.md (and the legacy tree's .json), held equal to the delta's engine list by a test
decisions.why: Fixes a gate that let pool-only changes through ungated (a check passing unchecked work, 2026-11-18 fix-as-we-go); the test only fails when the stamp's area drifts from the engine list, enforcement of the fix.

decisions.summary: lands after T219 and before T220
decisions.why: Sequencing; puts the budget review in force before the pipeline stage's counters (T220) and the step-3b work they feed.

decisions.summary: checklist item 12: the old recipe passed every push unchecked, a defect
decisions.why: A check that passes bad work is a defect under constitution XIV v2.36.0 / the GM 2026-11-19; the red-first fixture (a stage accepted far under its count, which the old recipe passed) shows the wrong outcome.

decisions.summary: polder waterward counting ~1/20 of its accepted figure, counters possibly missing work, filed as T226; pipeline counters owed by T220
decisions.why: Neither is part of T224's subject (the review and the stamp); the waterward counters are a suspected, unconfirmed engine-counter defect, filed rather than carried silently, and the pipeline counters are already T220's. Per the GM's 2026-11-18 rule T226 must be settled before the next step's port begins; the block gives it no position, which does not block this task but is owed by the step's close.

decisions.summary: The pool walk is rebuilt from T219's derivation in a new gate crate `pool` with the phase guard on: each tree, tier and map folder listed once, each entry classified once, no git index read.
decisions.why: This is the GM's 2026-11-19 instruction to rebuild from derivations rather than port the Python's mistakes, under the 2026-10-30 rule against re-implementing the old algorithms. It is held to the derivation's budget.

decisions.summary: Every consumer that walked the pool on its own moves onto the one walk in this landing: reviews owed, measure probe, trials, review-gate.sh, mode_a's sweep/census/recorded-map/fixture checks, arbiter sheet edits and the depiction bundle.
decisions.why: One walk for every consumer is how the rebuilt walk replaces the per-tool re-walks that the efficiency rule targets. It drops no consumer and no case.

decisions.summary: pool/index.html is written by Rust from the walk, grouped by tree and tier, and lists all 30 maps where the old index listed 6 (the six Mode A sheets).
decisions.why: An index that hides 24 of 30 maps from its reader is a wrong outcome, so it is a defect under constitution XIV and the GM's 2026-11-18 rule to fix as we go. Listing all 30 widens; nothing is narrowed. Both figures carry one-shot labels.

decisions.summary: A folder with only a .gen.py (no spec, compound or svg) is no longer classified as a sheet.
decisions.why: The class comes from the derivation, not from the Python. It was measured on 2026-11-19 by testing every folder of both trees, and no real folder falls in it, so the sweep, census and reviews owed reach every map they reached before. A difference from the Python that loses no real map is not a defect and narrows nothing, and a .gen.py-only sheet is Python that FR-001 removes anyway.

decisions.summary: A live folder with a manifest and no spec or compound is no longer a map.
decisions.why: The same one-shot measurement on 2026-11-19 tested every folder of both trees for a manifest with no spec or compound and found none, and the walk reports no unclassified real folder. No map any check reached drops out, so this is the derivation's definition, not a narrowing of what is swept.

decisions.summary: A spec-only hamlet is now counted as a map.
decisions.why: This widens what the checks reach, under the derivation's definition. No ruling is owed.

decisions.summary: The walk counts under the derivation's kind names behind a `counters` feature. This landing counts pool 332 and legacy 170, and the rest of the derivation's 1,894 pool budget is T221's.
decisions.why: The derivation's budget is split across tasks, not dropped: the remainder is assigned to T221 by name. The 332 and 170 carry one-shot labels, and 1,894 is cited as T219's derived budget rather than an observation.

decisions.summary: One writer per tree until T222 (FR-003): on main, render-sync's Python alone writes pool/index.html, because render_cache.py imports the old index and renders main; in a clone, the Rust writer alone writes it through sync-in.
decisions.why: FR-003 is the spec's guard against a piece's two implementations deciding the same output. With one writer per tree, no tree's index has two writers. The Python on main is kept because a not-yet-ported piece (render_cache.py) imports it, which is what FR-003's first clause requires. The main half is observed from render-sync's log (a one-shot label). The clone half (sync-in only) is asserted rather than measured, and the walk's tests and T222 should keep that true. Nothing in the GM's request forbids a staged cut-over.

decisions.summary: Main's pool/index.html keeps listing 6 of 30 maps, through the kept Python, until T222 moves main onto the Rust, and T221 comes before T222.
decisions.why: The GM's rule (2026-11-18) is per step: 'fix all known bugs in each step before moving on to porting the next step'. In request.md a 'step' is a unit of the port's plan (steps 1, 2, 3a, 3b), with pieces and phase tasks inside it, so a step is not a single task. T220, T221 and T222 are tasks of one rebuild from T219's single derivation: T221 holds 'the rest of the pool's 1,894' of that derivation's budget, and T222 moves main onto the Rust writer and deletes the old index. The defect is therefore closed inside the step that found it, before any next step's port begins. Ordering T227 before T221 is stricter than a per-step rule needs, and it narrows nothing. If T221 or T222 were later moved out of T219's derivation, the kept Python's index would owe the fix first.

decisions.summary: Deleting the old index's Python moves from T220 to T222.
decisions.why: It is still imported by render_cache.py, which renders main until T222, so deleting it now would break a live consumer that FR-002 says must keep working. FR-001's removal is deferred to a named task, not dropped. The bundle does not carry T222's line, so this was judged on the block's own statement.

decisions.summary: The heredoc guard-file bypass found during T220 is filed as T227, which lands before T221 begins. Order: after T224, then T227, then T221 and T222.
decisions.why: A guard that passes a guard-file rewrite is a defect, a check passing bad work. Ordering its fix before the next task's work begins satisfies the GM's fix-as-we-go rule. The bundle does not carry T227's line, so this was judged on the block's items 5 and 'Found and left?'.

decisions.summary: Exits and done-measure: the crate and consumer tests (exact counts on a fixture tree, every real folder classified), make quick/static/counters-inert/hooks-test green, and `make pool-index` writing 30 maps.
decisions.why: These are verification that enforces what the step asks for. They narrow nothing.

decisions.summary: The make-only guard's shell-write rule resolves each command's write targets through the shared shell walk (its own cds, the event's working directory for relative names) and checks each against held(), keeping the text patterns for what the walk cannot see
decisions.why: T220 found the guard passing shell writes of held files (87 of 156, then 141 of 210 forms missed, dated and methoded): a check passing bad work is a defect, and the GM 2026-11-18 asked that known bugs be fixed in each step before the next. The change only makes the existing refusal reach the files it already holds; it adds no new held file and no new refusal class.

decisions.summary: The walk learns perl -i, sed --in-place=, a quoted script with a space, rsync's destination, dd of= and truncate's files, each red first
decisions.why: Each is a write form the matrix showed passing a held-file write; covering it is the same defect fix. Measured 0 of 210 missed after.

decisions.summary: Two false refusals the walk fixes (a cd into tests/hooks then a new suite; a scratch settings.json) move to permit in the corpus, their old verdicts kept
decisions.why: A guard refusing correct work is fixed in its port and its case's expected result changed as fixed (FR-002's exception, constitution XIV); the block does not cite FR-002 by id but does what it says.

decisions.summary: Names fed through xargs are not detected, recorded in docs/guards.md
decisions.why: Scoped to the block's own stated reason: names the guard cannot know before the command runs (produced at run time by find, ls, a file's contents). A guard reading the command text before execution physically cannot know them, and refusing every xargs-fed write instead would refuse correct work and break the cited rule to match invocations, not mentions. This ruling does not cover a held name spelled literally in the command text and piped into xargs; such a name is visible before the command runs and falls outside the exception as worded.

decisions.summary: A target written through a variable the command does not set is not detected, recorded in docs/guards.md
decisions.why: Scoped to names whose value the guard cannot know before the command runs: the variable's value is not in the command and shell state does not persist between calls. It does not cover a held name spelled literally after a variable (e.g. a literal Makefile or .claude/settings.json suffix), which is visible in the text and outside the exception as worded.

decisions.summary: make guard-edit refusing dev/work-budget.json while the refusals point to it is added to T225, which lands before T221
decisions.why: A known defect (a tool refusing valid input) carried to a task ordered to land before the next step (T221), so it is fixed before moving on as the GM asked 2026-11-18. Verified from the block's own statement only; T225's line is not in the bundle.

decisions.summary: Whether the guards' own sources should be held is left to the GM through escalation-check
decisions.why: Holding more files would be new refusing behavior nobody asked for; leaving it as a question narrows nothing the GM asked.

decisions.summary: Instructions to run `make <name>` checked by script over guard and gate message strings, agent files, docs/, dev/*.md, the CLAUDE.md files and the .specify templates; history (specs, run logs, fixtures, retirement notes) left as written.
decisions.why: A tip naming a command that does not run is a wrong outcome (constitution XIV), fixed as found under the GM's 2026-11-18 'fix all known bugs in each step'. Leaving history as written is not a narrowing: a record of what was run is not an instruction, and nothing in the request asks history rewritten.

decisions.summary: Live text re-pointed at the command that does the job now: the round-arbiter agent file, l7r/diagram/tools/CLAUDE.md, docs/efficiency-tooling.md, docs/guards.md, docs/session-clones.md, docs/spec-kit-and-reviews.md, dev/lessons.md, the .specify templates, and the dev/work-budget.json guard-file refusals naming `make budget-change`.
decisions.why: Re-pointing a tip at the command that does its job fixes the defect without changing what the tooling enforces; this is the fix-as-we-go rule applied.

decisions.summary: pair_hooks' gate pattern matches `make done` only.
decisions.why: Rests on the block's premise that the other names it matched no longer exist as rules; a pattern on a dead command matches nothing, so narrowing it to the live command removes no enforcement.

decisions.summary: measure_hooks' `make perf` reminder and `make test-full` detection removed; its cadence keyed on `make done` and `make done FULL=1`.
decisions.why: Rests on the block's premise that `make perf` and `make test-full` no longer exist (the perf family is also among the constitution's dead commands the block lists). The block gives no line on whether some live command does the perf reminder's job; it states the rule 're-pointed at the command that does the job now, or removed', so if one exists the reminder is re-pointed, not removed. Nothing in the request or spec asks for a perf reminder, so removing a tip to a dead command narrows nothing asked.

decisions.summary: The work-budget bundle's `make perf-fanout` refusal removed.
decisions.why: Rests on the block's premise that nothing writes that report now: a refusal demanding an unwritable report refuses correct work, which FR-002's one exception has fixed in place, its suite case's expected result changed in the same commit and named.

decisions.summary: The cohort note and the land's `make rust-gate` call removed.
decisions.why: Rests on the block's premise that the call is unreachable at rust-only; removing unreachable code and a note to a dead command changes no behavior.

decisions.summary: The .specify templates' box titles kept so existing checklists still satisfy `make land`.
decisions.why: Keeps existing work valid; changes nothing the GM asked for.

decisions.summary: A make-only suite check, red first, refuses any `make <name>` in a guard or gate message or an agent file that names no rule (14 on HEAD, 2026-11-19, none now).
decisions.why: Enforcement of the fix: delete the defect fix and the check has nothing left to check. It serves the GM's 2026-11-18 'fix all known bugs' and the XIV rule that a fix is pinned; its reach (messages and agent files) is narrower than the fix, not wider.

decisions.summary: The constitution's six dead commands (`make maps`, `make full-hamlet-sweep`, `make roll-audit`, `make perf-ab`, `make perf SCALING=1`, `make perf-report`) left in this task; an amendment put to the GM through escalation-check.
decisions.why: These are known defects by the block's own item 12, and 'fix all known bugs in each step' (2026-11-18) reaches them. But the session cannot amend the constitution alone: the GM's own 2026-11-18 words ('we should definitely amend our project guidelines and speckit constitution') show amendments are made at his word, so the fix is routed to the one authority that can make it, not dropped. Legitimate only as the block states it: the escalation-check question is filed by this task; a mention with no question filed would be a defect left and NOT LEGITIMATE.

decisions.summary: dev/rust-tooling.md's Python-era rows left as history.
decisions.why: An inventory a gate reads, whose rows record what existed; history is left as written under the same rule as the scope decision, and no reader is told to run them.

decisions.summary: The check cannot see a command name assembled from pieces; the one known instance (pair_hooks') fixed by hand.
decisions.why: A stated limit of the enforcing check with no known defect left behind it: the one instance found is fixed. Not a narrowing of the fix, which reaches every instance found.

decisions.summary: Lands after T227, before T221, in one landing.
decisions.why: Sequencing only.

decisions.summary: The driver and cache are rebuilt from derivations/T219-pipeline.md with the phase guard on, in the pool crate, not ported from the Python cache.
decisions.why: The GM 2026-11-19 ('rebuilding from derivations, not porting the Python's mistakes') and the 2026-10-30 rule against re-implementing the old algorithms ask for exactly this.

decisions.summary: One read table per clone keyed by stat with the racy-file rule; a changed read removes every map entry its row names durably before taking the new digest; publish by rename with the meta last; engines identified by GNU build id; font set by directory and file stats; table locked for the run.
decisions.why: Implementation design serving FR-001 and the efficiency rule; it narrows no clause and is aimed at the stated goal that no map is served from content it was not built from.

decisions.summary: The legacy tree is always FROZEN; REGEN_FROZEN=1 and PROFILE=1 go with the deleted Python engine they acted on.
decisions.why: The knobs acted only on Python engine files this task deletes (FR-001); nothing in the request asks for frozen legacy sheets to stay regenerable, and FR-002 lets a tool's usage differ so long as it does its job for its callers. A removed debug switch is not a wrong outcome.

decisions.summary: make map MAP=<folder|file|name> and MAP=--all run any pool map, hamlets included, printing CACHED, REGENERATED with reason, or FROZEN; GEN= is refused naming the MAP= form.
decisions.why: make stays the one entry point (FR-005); a usage change is allowed by FR-002, and the refusal points the caller at the new form, so callers still get their job done. Hamlets being drawable widens rather than narrows.

decisions.summary: Engines draw into a staging folder; Mode A reports looked-for-but-missing files as reads; a read changed during a run leaves the map drawn but unpublished so the next run redraws it; both pinned red first.
decisions.why: Fixes two named defects of the old key (a sheet left stale when a looked-for file is created later; a race), which the GM's 2026-11-18 'fix all known bugs in each step' asks for. These are wrong outcomes (a stale map served), not mere differences.

decisions.summary: The six .gen.py, interactive/sheet.py, pipeline/regen.py and pipeline/rollcache.py are deleted unread; bundle_door's is_current asks the cache in process.
decisions.why: FR-001 (every Python file replaced) and FR-003 (replacement passes, then the Python goes; no piece runs both).

decisions.summary: New since the last CLEAR: render_cache.py's own index, which finds maps by .gen.py, would now list nothing, so sync-with-main.sh writes the Rust index (make pool-index, 30 maps) after render-sync under the same lock until T222 deletes render_cache.py and that line.
decisions.why: It fixes a defect this task's deletions caused (an empty index page is a wrong outcome for its readers) in the same task instead of carrying it, as FR-002 ('what a caller reads of it ... it still finds') and the GM's 'fix all known bugs in each step' require. The bridge is temporary, its end named (T222), and T222 lands before T158 and before the next step's port, so nothing is left broken across a step boundary. It narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: New since the last CLEAR: no before-and-after page is published because no drawn sheet changed - the four hand sheets match main's and the two generated sheets differ only by the old render cache's stamp comment (observed 2026-11-19 by cmp and a line diff).
decisions.why: The request attaches the page to the engine slice, not to each task: 'each engine slice publishes a page of every pool sheet before and after' (request.md, 2026-11-17, 'the engine slices worked deliberately'). Whatever page the step owes falls due at the slice's close (T158), and this block does not take it away. Read that way, the block's 'no before-and-after page is owed' means none is owed by this task, and in that reading it narrows nothing. Its limit: the label's comparison covers six sheets, four hand sheets and two generated ones, while the block also says render-sync drew every live map and the pool index lists 30. The bundle does not show that those six are every pool sheet the slice's page must cover. So this decision does NOT stand as proof that no pool sheet moved, and it does NOT excuse the slice's page at T158. A byte comparison offered as evidence of no change is not held as a standard here.

decisions.summary: A warm all-hit run counts pool 1,589 against budget 1,894 and legacy 170 against 170; warm --all 0.1 s, cold 22.6 s.
decisions.why: Holds the derivation's work budget, which is what the GM's 2026-10-30 efficiency rule and the 2026-11-19 plan ask for. Each figure carries a dated method label.

decisions.summary: gencache.py and _census.py stay because main's render_cache.py imports them until T222 deletes all three.
decisions.why: FR-003: Python stays until what reads it is replaced. The deletion is put off to T222 inside the same step, before T158 and before the next step's port, so FR-001's reach is not narrowed.

decisions.summary: New since the last CLEAR: after T227 and T225, then T229 (a guard fix, no port), then T222, both landing before T158 (the step's close) and before the next step's port.
decisions.why: This is the order the GM's 2026-11-18 rule requires: each step's known defects are fixed before the next step's port begins.

decisions.summary: Checks still reading what no longer exists (measure probe's pool changes matching nothing, preflight's roll-census read, land's census variable filter) and whether one failing map should stop render-sync are put on T222's line; the Python cache's old .gencache/<map>/ entries are left on disk.
decisions.why: A check that matches nothing passes everything, which counts as a defect, but it goes to T222 inside this step, before T158 and the next port, which satisfies 'fix all known bugs in each step before moving on'. The stale .gencache entries are a one-time remnant that nothing writes to or reads any more. No map, check or tool gives a wrong outcome because of them, and FR-013 covers what the tooling keeps making, not a past pile, so this is a leftover, not a defect.

decisions.summary: Every map regenerates once on the first run (new cache); a spec edit now counts as drawing code for reviews owed; make verify and the review gate draw hamlets too.
decisions.why: Consequences of the sound read set the GM's rebuild asks for: a spec a map reads is an input of that map. These widen coverage and narrow nothing that was asked.
